# ❌ WRONG - individual test files listed in a top-level test target
sources += [ "//brave/components/ai_chat/core/credential_manager_unittest.cc" ]

# ❌ WRONG - component :unit_tests dep added to brave_unit_tests in test/BUILD.gn
#            when it doesn't need chrome/browser-layer test support
# test/BUILD.gn -> test("brave_unit_tests")
deps += [ "//brave/components/brave_vpn/browser/v2:unit_tests" ]
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - test target lives in the component's own BUILD.gn
# components/brave_vpn/browser/v2/BUILD.gn
source_set("unit_tests") {
  testonly = true
  sources = [ "..._unittest.cc" ]
  deps = [ ... ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - aggregated by brave_components_unittests in components/BUILD.gn
# components/BUILD.gn -> test("brave_components_unittests")
deps += [ "//brave/components/brave_vpn/browser/v2:unit_tests" ]

title: Create `test_support` Targets for Reusable Fakes/Mocks
summary: When creating fake or mock implementations of services for testing, put them in a separate `test_support` BUILD.gn target rather than embedding them directly in a `unit_tests` target.

title: Use `PlatformBrowserTest` for Cross-Platform Browser Tests
summary: Browser tests that should run on both desktop and Android should use `PlatformBrowserTest` as the base class instead of `InProcessBrowserTest`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
class MyBrowserTest : public InProcessBrowserTest {};
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
class MyBrowserTest : public PlatformBrowserTest {};

title: Use `public_deps` for Header-File Includes in BUILD.gn
summary: When a dependency's headers are included in your target's header files (not just .cc files), that dependency must be listed in `public_deps`, not `deps`.
body:
**When a dependency's headers are included in your target's header files (not
just .cc files), that dependency must be listed in `public_deps`, not `deps`.**
This ensures consumers of your target also get the transitive include paths they
need.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - header-visible dependency in regular deps
source_set("my_service") {
  sources = [ "my_service.h", "my_service.cc" ]
  deps = [ "//components/prefs" ]  # prefs is used in my_service.h!
}

# ✅ CORRECT - header dependency in public_deps
source_set("my_service") {
  sources = [ "my_service.h", "my_service.cc" ]
  public_deps = [ "//components/prefs" ]  # used in header
  deps = [ "//base" ]  # only used in .cc
}
```

title: Utility Scripts Should Be Python, Not Node.js or Shell
summary: Build and utility scripts in brave-core should be written in Python (using `vpython` from depot tools), not Node.js or shell scripts.
body:
**Build and utility scripts in brave-core should be written in Python (using
`vpython` from depot tools), not Node.js or shell scripts.** This follows
Chromium conventions, avoids additional runtime dependencies, and works on all
platforms including Windows.

title: Unconditional Buildflags Deps with Conditional `deps +=`
summary: When adding `deps +=` inside an `if(enable_feature)` block in GN, always add an unconditional `buildflags` dependency outside the conditional.
body:
**When adding `deps +=` inside an `if(enable_feature)` block in GN, always add
an unconditional `buildflags` dependency outside the conditional.** The
buildflags header is needed even when the feature is disabled (for the
`#if BUILDFLAG(...)` check itself). Run `gn check` with the buildflag disabled
to verify.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - buildflags dep only inside conditional
if (enable_brave_rewards) {
  deps += [
    "//brave/components/brave_rewards/common/buildflags",
    "//brave/components/brave_rewards/browser",
  ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - buildflags dep unconditional
deps += [
  "//brave/components/brave_rewards/common/buildflags",
]
if (enable_brave_rewards) {
  deps += [ "//brave/components/brave_rewards/browser" ]
}
```

title: Use source_set Only for Internal Targets (with Restricted Visibility)
summary: Public targets for a component should use `static_library` or `component`, not `source_set`.
body:
**Public targets for a component should use `static_library` or `component`, not
`source_set`.** Only internal deps should use `source_set`, and those must have
restricted visibility to prevent external use.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - internal source_set with default (public) visibility
source_set("internal_network") {
  sources = [ ... ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - restricted visibility
source_set("internal_network") {
  visibility = [ ":*" ]  # Only usable within this BUILD.gn
  sources = [ ... ]
}
```

title: Python File Writes: Use `newline='\n'`
summary: When writing files from Python scripts, always specify `newline='\n'`
body:
**When writing files from Python scripts, always specify `newline='\n'`** in
`open()` to ensure consistent LF line endings across platforms (especially
Windows).

```python
# ❌ WRONG - platform-dependent line endings
with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

# ✅ CORRECT - consistent LF endings
with open(output_path, 'w', newline='\n') as f:
    f.write(content)
```
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - platform-dependent line endings
with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - consistent LF endings
with open(output_path, 'w', newline='\n') as f:
    f.write(content)

title: Use `include_rules` for Common Includes, `specific_include_rules` for Edge Cases
summary: In DEPS files, use `include_rules` for generally allowed includes across all files in a directory.
body:
**In DEPS files, use `include_rules` for generally allowed includes across all
files in a directory.** Reserve `specific_include_rules` for edge cases where an
include should only be allowed in specific files.

```python
# ❌ WRONG - using specific_include_rules for commonly needed includes
specific_include_rules = {
  ".*\.cc": [
    "+brave/components/content_settings/core/common",
    "+brave/components/content_settings/core/browser",
  ],
}

# ✅ CORRECT - include_rules for generally allowed includes
include_rules = [
  "+brave/components/content_settings/core/common",
  "+brave/components/content_settings/core/browser",
]
```
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - include_rules for generally allowed includes
include_rules = [
  "+brave/components/content_settings/core/common",
  "+brave/components/content_settings/core/browser",
]

title: Bump `resource_ids.spec` by 5
summary: When adding new resource IDs in `resource_ids.spec`, bump the next ID by 5 (not 1)
body:
**When adding new resource IDs in `resource_ids.spec`, bump the next ID by 5
(not 1)** to leave room for additions without conflicting with adjacent entries.

title: Use `component()` Not `static_library()` for Service GN Targets
summary: Mojo service targets should use `component()` instead of `static_library()` in BUILD.gn.
body:
**Mojo service targets should use `component()` instead of `static_library()` in
BUILD.gn.** Components support dynamic linking and are the correct target type
for service implementations.

title: Unit Tests for Components Must NOT Live in Browser
summary: Unit tests for code in `//brave/components` must not be placed in `//brave/browser`.
body:
**Unit tests for code in `//brave/components` must not be placed in
`//brave/browser`.** Tests should live alongside the code they test. Use
`content::RenderViewHostTestHarness` for component-level tests that need content
layer support.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - component test in browser directory
# browser/ai_chat/associated_link_content_unittest.cc
# testing code from components/ai_chat/content/browser/

# ✅ CORRECT - test alongside the code
# components/ai_chat/content/browser/associated_link_content_unittest.cc
source_set("unit_tests") {
  sources = [ "associated_link_content_unittest.cc" ]
}
```
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - component test in browser directory
# browser/ai_chat/associated_link_content_unittest.cc
# testing code from components/ai_chat/content/browser/

title: DEPS Allowlist Paths Must Exactly Match Include Paths
summary: DEPS file allowlist paths must exactly match the `#include` paths used in source files.
body:
**DEPS file allowlist paths must exactly match the `#include` paths used in
source files.** A mismatch (e.g., `common/` vs `core/`) means the DEPS check
doesn't validate the right file.

title: Use `assert()` at Top of Entire-Feature BUILD.gn Files
summary: If an entire BUILD.gn file belongs to a feature, use `assert(enable_feature)` at the top

title: Don't Confuse Feature Flags with Build Flags
summary: Runtime feature flags (`base::FeatureList`) and compile-time build flags (`BUILDFLAG()`) are completely different mechanisms.
body:
**Runtime feature flags (`base::FeatureList`) and compile-time build flags
(`BUILDFLAG()`) are completely different mechanisms.** Do not confuse them in
either direction: runtime feature flags cannot gate build-time deps, and
buildflag-guarded code does not need a redundant runtime feature flag on top.

- **Build flags** (e.g., `enable_brave_wallet`, `BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_EXTENSIONS)`)
  are set at compile time via GN args. They can guard `deps`, `sources`,
  `#include` blocks, and code blocks.
- **Feature flags** (e.g., `base::FeatureList::IsEnabled(kMyFeature)`) are
  checked at runtime. They can only guard code execution, not build-time
  dependency inclusion.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - runtime feature flag cannot gate build-time deps
if (kLocalAIModels) {  # Does not exist in GN!
  deps += [ "//brave/components/local_ai/resources" ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - use a build flag if one exists
if (enable_local_ai) {
  deps += [ "//brave/components/local_ai/resources" ]
}

# ✅ ALSO CORRECT - if no build flag exists yet, don't invent one
# Include deps unconditionally and let runtime feature checks handle enablement
deps += [ "//brave/components/local_ai/resources" ]
```
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - runtime feature flag cannot gate build-time deps
if (kLocalAIModels) {  # Does not exist in GN!
  deps += [ "//brave/components/local_ai/resources" ]
}
right:
# ✅ ALSO CORRECT - if no build flag exists yet, don't invent one
# Include deps unconditionally and let runtime feature checks handle enablement
deps += [ "//brave/components/local_ai/resources" ]

title: Don't Use `nogncheck` - Fix the Underlying Dep Guard
summary: Do not use `nogncheck` to suppress gn check failures.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - suppressing the real problem
#include "brave/components/foo/bar.h"  // nogncheck
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - fix the GN dep to be properly guarded
// Ensure the dep is conditionally added in BUILD.gn

title: GN Deps Guarded by Feature Flags Only, Not Platform Guards
summary: Within a single GN target, deps should be added behind the relevant buildflags only, not nested inside platform guards.

title: Don't Guard Deps with Unrelated Guards
summary: A dep should only be placed inside a guard if the dep itself is specific to that guard condition.
body:
**A dep should only be placed inside a guard if the dep itself is specific to
that guard condition.** If a dep is needed regardless of the guard condition,
include it unconditionally. Putting unrelated deps inside guards (e.g., placing
a general utility dep inside `if (use_blink)` or `if (!is_ios)` when it has
nothing to do with blink/iOS) creates incorrect build configurations and can
cause missing symbol errors on platforms where the guard evaluates to false.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - "//brave/components/constants" has nothing to do with blink
if (use_blink) {
  deps += [
    "//brave/components/constants",
    "//content/public/browser",
  ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - only guard deps that actually relate to the guard
deps += [
  "//brave/components/constants",
]
if (use_blink) {
  deps += [ "//content/public/browser" ]
}
```

title: When Disabling a Feature, Compile Out Its Tests
summary: When a build flag disables a feature, exclude the feature-specific test files from the build
body:
**When a build flag disables a feature, exclude the feature-specific test files
from the build** using conditionals rather than trying to fix compilation errors
by adjusting test dependencies.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - fixing deps to make disabled feature tests compile
deps += [ "//brave/components/brave_rewards" ]  # just for tests

# ✅ CORRECT - compile out disabled feature tests
if (enable_brave_rewards) {
  sources += [ "rewards_service_unittest.cc" ]
}
```
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - fixing deps to make disabled feature tests compile
deps += [ "//brave/components/brave_rewards" ]  # just for tests

title: Build Flag Validation Requires Both States
summary: When adding a build flag, run `gn_check`, unit tests, component tests, browser tests, and presubmit with the flag both enabled AND disabled.
body:
**When adding a build flag, run `gn_check`, unit tests, component tests, browser
tests, and presubmit with the flag both enabled AND disabled.** Issues
frequently only appear in the disabled state.

title: Use Chromium UI Preprocessor for Conditional WebUI Code
summary: Use `// <if expr="enable_feature">` in JS and `<if expr="enable_feature">` in HTML to conditionally compile feature-specific WebUI code.

title: Assert Build Flag Dependencies Between Features
summary: When Feature A depends on Feature B, assert Feature B's build flag is true when Feature A is enabled
body:
**When Feature A depends on Feature B, assert Feature B's build flag is true
when Feature A is enabled** rather than making Feature A work without Feature B
for unsupported configurations.

```gn
# In brave/components/brave_rewards/BUILD.gn
assert(enable_brave_wallet,
       "Rewards requires Wallet (enable_brave_wallet=true)")
```

title: Share Constants via Common Headers
summary: Shared constants (like limits, URLs, keys) should be defined in a common header

title: Never Add Anything to `components/constants` (Deprecated)
summary: The `components/constants` directory is not a real component — it is a deprecated legacy dumping ground that should be removed.
body:
**The `components/constants` directory is not a real component — it is a
deprecated legacy dumping ground that should be removed.** Never add new
constants, headers, or targets there. Instead, place constants in a `common`
target within the component that owns them.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - adding to the legacy catch-all
# components/constants/brave_constants.h
inline constexpr char kGate3OAuthUrl[] = "...";

# ✅ CORRECT - in the owning component's common target
# components/brave_rewards/common/constants.h
inline constexpr char kGate3OAuthUrl[] = "...";
```

Do not add new `deps` on `//brave/components/constants` either — migrate
existing usages to proper component-owned targets when you encounter them.

If a constant (especially a URL) is shared across multiple components with no
clear owner, place it in a `brave_domains` target.

title: Don't Use Compound Buildflags (Channel + Platform + Official)
summary: Do not create buildflags that combine channel, platform, and official_build conditions
body:
**Do not create buildflags that combine channel, platform, and official_build
conditions** (e.g., enabled only on nightly + desktop + official). These
compound flags break during branch migration (nightly → beta → release) and
create configurations that are nearly impossible to test locally. Use separate,
independently testable flags instead.

title: Use `public` to Restrict Header Visibility in Components
summary: When a GN target exposes only a subset of its headers to consumers, explicitly list those headers in `public = [...]` to keep the rest internal.
body:
**When a GN target exposes only a subset of its headers to consumers, explicitly
list those headers in `public = [...]` to keep the rest internal.** This
improves encapsulation — consumers can only include the declared public headers,
preventing accidental coupling to implementation details.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - all headers are implicitly public
source_set("core") {
  sources = [
    "local_ai_service.h",
    "local_ai_service.cc",
    "internal_helper.h",
    "internal_helper.cc",
  ]
  deps = [ ... ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - only the service header is public, internals are hidden
source_set("core") {
  public = [ "local_ai_service.h" ]
  sources = [
    "local_ai_service.h",
    "local_ai_service.cc",
    "internal_helper.h",
    "internal_helper.cc",
  ]
  deps = [ ... ]
}
```

This is especially useful for `static_library` and `source_set` targets that
contain both a public API and private implementation files. GN will enforce that
only headers listed in `public` can be `#include`d by dependent targets.
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - only the service header is public, internals are hidden
source_set("core") {
  public = [ "local_ai_service.h" ]
  sources = [
    "local_ai_service.h",
    "local_ai_service.cc",
    "internal_helper.h",
    "internal_helper.cc",
  ]
  deps = [ ... ]
}

title: Add New Endpoints to the HSTS Pin List
summary: When adding any new Brave endpoint, it must be added to the HSTS pin list
body:
**When adding any new Brave endpoint, it must be added to the HSTS pin list** in
`chromium_src/net/tools/transport_security_state_generator/input_file_parsers.cc`.
New endpoints must be added to both the pins `"entries"` list and the HSTS
`"entries"` list in that file. This applies to all new endpoints regardless of
whether they require user opt-in.

title: Don't Add New Source Files to `browser/ui/BUILD.gn`
summary: Don't add new `sources` entries to the `source_set("ui")` target in `brave/browser/ui/BUILD.gn`.
body:
**Don't add new `sources` entries to the `source_set("ui")` target in
`brave/browser/ui/BUILD.gn`.** Adding source files here is flagged in review
because `//chrome/browser/ui` is prone to circular dependencies, and Brave
should avoid adding to that problem. Place the new files in a more specific,
lower-level target instead.

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - new source files added to source_set("ui") in brave/browser/ui/BUILD.gn
source_set("ui") {
  sources = [
    ...
    "webui/history/brave_history_embeddings_page_handler.cc",
    "webui/history/brave_history_embeddings_page_handler.h",
  ]
}

# ✅ CORRECT - put the files in a feature-specific lower-level target
# e.g. brave/browser/ui/webui/history/BUILD.gn
source_set("history") {
  sources = [
    "brave_history_embeddings_page_handler.cc",
    "brave_history_embeddings_page_handler.h",
  ]
  deps = [ ... ]
}
```

Break circular dependencies using the interface/impl pattern (public headers in
the direct dependency, implementation pulled into a higher-level target like
`//brave/browser`), dependency inversion, or the templated-subclass technique.
Only fall back to `brave_chrome_browser_ui_allow_circular_includes_from` /
`sources.gni` as a temporary last resort, and never use `check_includes = false`
to suppress circular include errors. See [`gni_sources.md`](../gni_sources.md)
(Circular dependencies).

title: Don't Use System-Absolute Paths in GN
summary: Targets that are part of the Brave build must never use system-absolute paths in GN. When calling `rebase_path()`, pass the path's expected base as `new_base`—usually `root_build_dir` for GN actions—so the generated Ninja file uses a relative, relocatable path.
body:
**Targets that are part of the Brave build must never use system-absolute paths
in GN. When calling `rebase_path()`, pass the path's expected base as
`new_base`—usually `root_build_dir` for GN actions—so the generated Ninja file
uses a relative, relocatable path.**

```gn
# ❌ WRONG - the default empty new_base produces a system-absolute path
args = [ "--output=" + rebase_path(output) ]

# ✅ CORRECT - rebase relative to the command's working directory
args = [ "--output=" + rebase_path(output, root_build_dir) ]
```

One-argument `rebase_path()` produces a system-absolute, checkout-specific path,
so never use it for a target that is part of the Brave build. Such paths can
interfere with remote build execution and fail when build artifacts are reused
from a cloned or relocated checkout. The exceptions are host-side tooling and
targets that generate wrapper scripts or configuration exclusively for local
developer use and never run on a remote bot worker. If a tool changes its
working directory, rebase to that directory rather than blindly using
`root_build_dir`. When a tool requires an absolute path, invoke it through a
wrapper script that receives relative path arguments and converts them to
absolute paths at runtime. See GN's
[`rebase_path()` reference](https://gn.googlesource.com/gn/+/master/docs/reference.md#func_rebase_path)
for the complete API contract.
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - the default empty new_base produces a system-absolute path
args = [ "--output=" + rebase_path(output) ]
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - rebase relative to the command's working directory
args = [ "--output=" + rebase_path(output, root_build_dir) ]

title: Avoid Modifying Chromium Source When Possible
summary: Changes to Chromium code in `src/` should be avoided whenever possible.
body:
**Changes to Chromium code in `src/` should be avoided whenever possible.**
Implement features and fixes entirely within brave-core (`src/brave/`) using
Brave's own code and APIs.

When Chromium changes are unavoidable, follow this preference order:

1. **chromium_src overrides** (strongly preferred) — Override files in
   `src/brave/chromium_src/` that replace or wrap upstream behavior at compile
   time. See the sections below for patterns and conventions.

2. **Patches** (last resort) — When a chromium_src override is not feasible
   (e.g., you need to add a `virtual` keyword where `#define` tricks don't work,
   or modify a GN file), directly edit the files in `src/` and then generate
   patches:

   ```bash
   cd src/brave
   pnpm run update_patches
```

   This reads the changes you made to files in `src/` and updates the
   corresponding patch files in `src/brave/patches/`. Always keep patches
   minimal — one-line additions are ideal.

title: Don't Use chromium_src Overrides to Disable Tests
summary: Never use `#define TestName DISABLED_TestName` in chromium_src overrides to disable upstream tests.
body:
**Never use `#define TestName DISABLED_TestName` in chromium_src overrides to
disable upstream tests.** Use filter files in `test/filters/` instead, and move
any Brave-specific replacement tests into the appropriate Brave test target
(`brave_unit_tests`, `brave_browser_tests`, `brave_components_unittests`).

title: Minimize Code Duplication in Overrides
summary: When overriding Chromium code via `chromium_src/`, prefer wrapping only the changed section and falling back to `ChromiumImpl` for everything else.

title: Prefer chromium_src Overrides Over Patches
summary: Always prefer a chromium_src override over adding a patch.

title: Never Copy Entire Files or Methods
summary: Never copy entire Chromium files or methods into chromium_src.

title: Prefer Subclassing Over Patching
summary: When possible, subclass Chromium classes using chromium_src overrides instead of patching.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - patching tab_strip.cc to change behavior
+  BraveNewTabButton* new_tab_button = new BraveNewTabButton(...);
// ❌ WRONG - patching IncognitoNewTabPageView directly
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - create BraveIncognitoNewTabPage as subclass
// Patch only changes the superclass reference

title: Always Use Original Header Paths
summary: In chromium_src overrides, always `#include` the original header path, not the chromium_src version.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
#include "brave/chromium_src/net/proxy_resolution/proxy_resolution_service.h"
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
#include "net/proxy_resolution/proxy_resolution_service.h"

title: Replace Entire Classes with Dummy chromium_src Files
summary: When you need to disable or replace a Chromium class entirely, create a minimal no-op dummy replacement in chromium_src for the `.h` and `.cc` files.

title: Don't Use `#define` to Add `virtual` — Use `make_virtual`
summary: When a Chromium method needs to be made virtual for override, use the `make_virtual` plaster rewriter, not a `#define` in a chromium_src header override.
body:
**When a Chromium method needs to be made virtual for override, use the
`make_virtual` plaster rewriter, not a `#define` in a chromium_src header
override.**

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - chromium_src define; rewrites every SomeMethod in the TU
#define SomeMethod virtual SomeMethod
#include "src/path/to/original_header.h"
#undef SomeMethod
```

```yaml
# ✅ CORRECT - rewrite/path/to/original_header.h.yaml
substitutions:
  - description: 'Let BraveSomeClass override SomeMethod.'
    make_virtual:
      class_name: SomeClass
      method_name: SomeMethod
```

The rewriter also handles what the `#define` could not: a pointer or reference
return type (`T* Method()`), and a destructor (quote it — `'~SomeClass'`). See
[PLSTR-003](./plaster.md#PLSTR-003).
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - rewrite/path/to/original_header.h.yaml
substitutions:
  - description: 'Let BraveSomeClass override SomeMethod.'
    make_virtual:
      class_name: SomeClass
      method_name: SomeMethod

title: Never Use `#define final` to Remove the `final` Keyword
summary: Redefining `final` via `#define` is undefined behavior per the C++ standard and is highly viral.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - use a minimal patch if no alternative exists
// Or use #define only for specific method names that won't collide

title: Add Explanation Comments in chromium_src Override Files
summary: When creating a chromium_src override, include comments explaining why the override is needed.
body:
**When creating a chromium_src override, include comments explaining why the
override is needed.** The override's purpose is not always self-evident from the
code alone. **NEVER require a global file-level comment if per-function comments
adequately explain the purpose.**

**Exception: NEVER request doc comments on method declarations injected inside
`#define` macros (e.g., macros that add virtual methods to an upstream class).**
Comments cannot be practically added inside macro bodies. If documentation is
needed, it belongs in the header file that defines the macro or in the
implementation file, not inline in the macro expansion.

```cpp
// chromium_src/chrome/browser/ui/views/tabs/tab_view.cc

// Add Brave-specific tab context menu items. The upstream class doesn't
// support extensibility here, so we replace the menu construction logic.
void TabView::BuildContextMenu() {
  ...
}
```

title: Verify chromium_src Header GN Dependencies
summary: When adding new `#include` directives in chromium_src override files, verify they have required GN dependencies.
body:
**When adding new `#include` directives in chromium_src override files, verify
they have required GN dependencies.** The override file is compiled as part of
the upstream target, which may not have deps on your Brave headers.

**How to verify:** Temporarily add the same headers to the original upstream
file and run `gn check`. If it fails, the upstream target needs the dependency
added (typically via a patch or `sources.gni`).

```bash
# Test: add the header to the original file temporarily, then:
gn check out/Default
# If it fails, the dep is missing
```

title: chromium_src Should Avoid Depending on Brave Targets
summary: A chromium_src override should avoid adding a GN dependency on, or a direct `#include` of, any downstream `//brave/...` target

title: Add Comments for Non-Obvious nullptr Assignments in chromium_src
summary: Add comments explaining non-obvious nullptr assignments in chromium_src overrides,
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - unclear why setting to nullptr
provider_ = nullptr;

title: Use `static_assert` to Protect Against Upstream Enum Changes
summary: When adding custom values after an upstream enum's last value, add a `static_assert`

title: Use `runtime_enabled_features.override.json5` for Blink Features
summary: When adding Brave-specific Blink runtime-enabled features, add them to `runtime_enabled_features.override.json5` instead of patching `runtime_enabled_features.json5`.
wrong: // ❌ WRONG - patching runtime_enabled_features.json5 (causes conflicts)

title: `chromium_src` Overrides Cannot Handle Private Methods in `.cc` Files
summary: The `chromium_src` override mechanism only works for symbols with external linkage.
right: // ✅ Use a .patch file to modify PrivateHelper directly

title: ⚠️ Override Replacement Strings Must Have Compatible Placeholders
summary: When creating a Brave replacement string that is substituted for an upstream string via `#undef`/`#define`, the replacement string must have compatible placeholders.
body:
**When creating a Brave replacement string that is substituted for an upstream
string via `#undef`/`#define`, the replacement string must have compatible
placeholders.** The upstream code calling the string supplies specific
placeholder values (`$1`, `$2`, etc.). If your replacement string has fewer
placeholders, extras are silently ignored. If it has more or different
placeholders, it can cause runtime errors. Always check what placeholders the
upstream caller provides and match them.

title: Guard Overridden String IDs with `#ifndef`/`#error`
summary: When overriding an upstream string ID via `#undef`/`#define`, add a compile-time guard to detect if the upstream ID is removed or renamed during a rebase.
body:
**When overriding an upstream string ID via `#undef`/`#define`, add a
compile-time guard to detect if the upstream ID is removed or renamed during a
rebase.** The `check_chromium_src.py` tool verifies symbols are still used in
the overridden file, but a `#ifndef`/`#error` guard provides an additional
safety net.

```cpp
// ✅ CORRECT - compile-time guard catches upstream removals
#ifndef IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS
#error "IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS is not defined"
#endif
#undef IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS
#define IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS \
  IDS_BRAVE_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE
```
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - compile-time guard catches upstream removals
#ifndef IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS
#error "IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS is not defined"
#endif
#undef IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS
#define IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS \
  IDS_BRAVE_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE

title: Fallback Methods Must Call the Correct Base Class
summary: When overriding a chromium_src fallback method, ensure the fallback calls the correct base class method.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use Existing Utilities Instead of Custom Code
summary: Always check for existing well-tested utilities before writing custom code.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use base::OnceCallback and base::BindOnce
summary: `base::Callback` and `base::Bind` are deprecated.
body:
**`base::Callback` and `base::Bind` are deprecated.** Use
`base::OnceCallback`/`base::RepeatingCallback` and
`base::BindOnce`/`base::BindRepeating`. Use `std::move` when passing or calling
a `base::OnceCallback`.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Never Use std::time - Use base::Time
summary: Always use `base::Time` and related classes instead of C-style `std::time`, `ctime`, or `time_t`.
body:
**Always use `base::Time` and related classes instead of C-style `std::time`,
`ctime`, or `time_t`.** The base library provides cross-platform, type-safe time
utilities.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `JSONValueConverter` for JSON/Type Conversion
summary: When parsing JSON into C++ types, prefer `base::JSONValueConverter` over manual key-by-key parsing.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use the Right Associative Container
summary: Chromium's container guidelines (`base/containers/README.md`) recommend specific containers for each use case.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - banned
std::unordered_map<std::string, double> feature_map_;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - default unordered container
absl::flat_hash_map<std::string, double> feature_map_;

// ✅ CORRECT - sorted, small/write-once
base::flat_map<std::string, int> lookup_;

// ✅ CORRECT - sorted, large, frequently mutated
std::map<std::string, int> large_mutable_lookup_;

// ✅ CORRECT - value pointer stability via unique_ptr wrapping
absl::flat_hash_map<Key, std::unique_ptr<Value>> stable_values;

// ✅ CORRECT - key pointer stability via node hash
absl::node_hash_map<std::string, int> stable_keys;

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Use Deprecated `GetAs*` Methods on `base::Value`
summary: The `GetAsString()`, `GetAsInteger()`, etc. methods on `base::Value` are deprecated.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
const std::string& str = value->GetString();

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `GetIfBool`/`GetIfInt`/`GetIfString` for Safe `base::Value` Access
summary: When extracting values from a `base::Value` where the type may not match, use `GetIf*` accessors instead of `Get*` which CHECK-fails on type mismatch.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - crashes if value is not a bool
if (value.GetBool()) { ... }
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - safe accessor with value_or
if (value.GetIfBool().value_or(false)) { ... }

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Use `std::to_string` - Use `base::NumberToString`
summary: `std::to_string` is on Chromium's deprecated list.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
std::string port_str = std::to_string(port);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
std::string port_str = base::NumberToString(port);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Use C-Style Casts
summary: Chromium prohibits C-style casts.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
double result = (double)integer_value / total;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
double result = static_cast<double>(integer_value) / total;

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Prefer std::move Over Clone
summary: Use `std::move` instead of cloning when you don't need the original value anymore.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Create Unnecessary Wrapper Types
summary: Don't create plural/container types when you can use arrays of the singular type.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - just use the vector directly
std::vector<MonthlyStatement> GetMonthlyStatements();

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use Pref Dict/List Values Directly
summary: Don't serialize to JSON strings when storing structured data in prefs.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `extern const char[]` Over `#define` for Strings
summary: Use `extern const char[]` instead of `#define` for string constants to keep them namespaced.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - pollutes preprocessor namespace
#define MY_URL "https://example.com"

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Prefer Enum Types Over String Constants for Typed Values
summary: When a value has a fixed set of valid options, use an enum with string conversion rather than passing raw strings.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - raw strings
void SetWalletType(const std::string& type);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: No C++ Exceptions in Third-Party Libraries
summary: C++ exceptions are disallowed in Chromium.
body:
**C++ exceptions are disallowed in Chromium.** When integrating third-party
libraries, verify they build with exception support disabled.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::EraseIf` / `std::erase_if` Instead of Manual Erase Loops
summary: Prefer `base::EraseIf` (for `base::flat_*` containers) or `std::erase_if` (for standard containers) over manual iterator-based erase loops.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::span` at API Boundaries Instead of `const std::vector&`
summary: Prefer `base::span<const T>` over `const std::vector<T>&` for function parameters that only read data.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - forces callers to use std::vector
void ProcessBuffer(const std::vector<uint8_t>& data);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - accepts any contiguous container
void ProcessBuffer(base::span<const uint8_t> data);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::FixedArray` Over `std::vector` for Known-Size Runtime Allocations
summary: When the size is known at creation but not at compile time, use `base::FixedArray`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - vector suggests dynamic resizing
std::vector<uint8_t> out(size);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - size is fixed after construction
base::FixedArray<uint8_t> out(size);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::HeapArray<uint8_t>` for Fixed-Size Byte Buffers
summary: When you need an owned byte buffer that won't be resized after creation, use `base::HeapArray<uint8_t>` instead of `std::vector<unsigned char>` or `std::vector<uint8_t>`.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::ToVector` for Range-to-Vector Conversions
summary: Use `base::ToVector(range)` instead of manual copy patterns when converting a range to a `std::vector`.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - base::ToVector
auto buffer = base::ToVector(base::span(kStaticData).first<sizeof(kStaticData) - 1>());

// ✅ CORRECT - with projection
auto names = base::ToVector(items, &Item::name);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Prefer Contiguous Containers Over Linked Lists
summary: Never use `std::list` for pure traversal — poor cache locality.
body:
**Never use `std::list` for pure traversal — poor cache locality.** Use
`std::list` only when stable iterators or frequent mid-container insert/remove
is required. Prefer `std::vector` with `reserve()` for known sizes.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `std::optional` Instead of Sentinel Values
summary: Never use empty string `""`, `-1`, or other magic values as sentinels for "no value".
body:
**Never use empty string `""`, `-1`, or other magic values as sentinels for "no
value".** Use `std::optional<T>`.

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - "" as sentinel for "no custom title"
void SetCustomTitle(const std::string& title);  // "" means "unset"

// ✅ CORRECT - explicit optionality
void SetCustomTitle(std::optional<std::string> title);  // nullopt means "unset"
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - "" as sentinel for "no custom title"
void SetCustomTitle(const std::string& title);  // "" means "unset"
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - explicit optionality
void SetCustomTitle(std::optional<std::string> title);  // nullopt means "unset"

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `.emplace()` for `std::optional` Initialization Clarity
summary: When engaging a `std::optional` member, prefer `.emplace()` for clarity about the intent.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - explicit engagement intent
elapsed_timer_.emplace();

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Return `std::optional` Instead of `bool` + Out Parameter
summary: When a function needs to return a value that may or may not exist, use `std::optional<T>` instead of returning `bool` with an out parameter.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
bool GetHistorySize(int* out_size);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
std::optional<int> GetHistorySize();

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `constexpr` for Compile-Time Constants
summary: Constants defined in anonymous namespaces should use `constexpr` instead of `const` when the value is known at compile time.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use Raw String Literals for Multiline Strings
summary: When embedding multiline strings (JavaScript, SQL, etc.), use raw string literals (`R"()"`) instead of escaping each line.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Pass Primitive Types by `const` Reference
summary: Primitive types (`int`, `bool`, `float`, pointers) should be passed by value, not by `const` reference.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
void ProcessItem(const int& id, const bool& enabled);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
void ProcessItem(int id, bool enabled);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Add `DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN` in New Code
summary: The `DISALLOW_COPY_AND_ASSIGN` macro is deprecated.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Declare Move Operations as `noexcept`
summary: When defining custom move constructors/assignment operators for structs used in `std::vector`, declare them `noexcept`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
Topic(Topic&&) = default;

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Avoid `std::optional<T>&` References
summary: Never pass `std::optional<T>&` as a function parameter.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - confusing, hidden copies
void Process(const std::optional<std::string>& value);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - take by value if storing
void Process(std::optional<std::string> value);

// ✅ CORRECT - use base::optional_ref for non-owning optional references
void Process(base::optional_ref<const std::string> value);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Short-Circuit on Non-HTTP(S) URLs
summary: In URL processing code (shields, debouncing, content settings), add an early return for non-HTTP/HTTPS URLs.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Narrow Integer Types in Setters or Parameters
summary: Setter and function parameter types must match the underlying field type.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Deprecate Prefs Before Removing Them
summary: When removing a preference that was previously stored in user profiles, first deprecate the pref (register it for clearing) in one release before fully removing it.
body:
**When removing a preference that was previously stored in user profiles, first
deprecate the pref (register it for clearing) in one release before fully
removing it.** This ensures the old value is cleared from existing profiles.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Modify Production Code Solely to Accommodate Tests
summary: NEVER let test-specific workarounds affect production behavior.
body:
**NEVER let test-specific workarounds affect production behavior.** Use test
infrastructure like `kHostResolverRules` command line switches in
`SetUpCommandLine` instead of adding production code paths only needed for
tests.

**NEVER flag a violation of this rule unless you are certain the code exists
solely for tests.** Clear signals include `CHECK_IS_TEST()`,
`#if defined(UNIT_TEST)`, `_for_testing` suffixes, or comments explicitly
mentioning test support. **NEVER flag legitimate production logic such as
handling empty/null/default values, reset paths, or cleanup behavior — these are
normal defensive coding patterns, not test accommodations. When uncertain, NEVER
flag.**

**Exception: NEVER flag thin `ForTesting()` accessors that expose internalized
features (e.g., `base::Feature`) under this rule.** These keep the feature
internalized while providing a clean way for tests to reference it, and do not
affect production behavior.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `url::kStandardSchemeSeparator` Instead of Hardcoded `"://"`
summary: When constructing URLs, use `url::kStandardSchemeSeparator` instead of the hardcoded string `"://"`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
std::string url = scheme + "://" + host + path;

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::DoNothing()` for No-Op Callbacks
summary: Use `base::DoNothing()` instead of empty lambdas when a no-op callback is needed.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - empty lambda
service->DoAsync([](const std::string&) {});
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
service->DoAsync(base::DoNothing());

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::StrAppend` Over `+= base::StrCat`
summary: When appending to an existing string, use `base::StrAppend(&str, {...})` instead of `str += base::StrCat({...})`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - temporary string then copy
result += base::StrCat({kOpenTag, "\n", "=== METADATA ===\n"});
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - append directly
base::StrAppend(&result, {kOpenTag, "\n", "=== METADATA ===\n"});

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `std::views::reverse()` for Reverse Iteration
summary: Prefer `std::views::reverse()` with range-based for loops over explicit reverse iterators.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `absl::StrFormat` Over `base::StringPrintf`
summary: Prefer `absl::StrFormat` for formatted string construction.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - deprecated
std::string msg = base::StringPrintf("Error %d: %s", code, desc.c_str());
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
std::string msg = absl::StrFormat("Error %d: %s", code, desc);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::saturated_cast` for Safe Numeric Conversions
summary: When converting between integer types, use `base::saturated_cast<TargetType>()` combined with `.value_or(default)` for safe, concise conversion of optional numeric values.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - overflow happens before the cast can help
size_t total = base::saturated_cast<size_t>(count * item_size);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - safe saturated cast with value_or
result = base::saturated_cast<uint64_t>(value.value_or(0));

// ✅ CORRECT - CHECK when the range is an invariant
uint8_t byte = base::checked_cast<uint8_t>(value_known_to_be_0_255);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `std::ranges` Algorithms Over Manual Loops
summary: Prefer C++20 `std::ranges::any_of`, `std::ranges::all_of`, `std::ranges::find_if` over manual for-loops with break conditions.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Guard `substr()` with Size Check
summary: Only call `substr()` when the content actually exceeds the limit.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - always creates a substring
std::string truncated = content.substr(0, max_length);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::expected<T, E>` Over Optional + Error Out-Parameter
summary: When a function can fail and needs to communicate error details, use `base::expected<T, E>` instead of `std::optional<T>` with a separate error out-parameter.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - separate error out-parameter
std::optional<Result> Parse(const std::string& input, std::string* error);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - base::expected bundles both
base::expected<Result, std::string> Parse(const std::string& input);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::MakeFixedFlatMap` for Static Enum-to-String Mappings
summary: For compile-time constant mappings between enums and strings, use `base::MakeFixedFlatMap`.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::JSONReader::ReadDict` for JSON Dictionary Parsing
summary: When parsing a JSON string expected to be a dictionary, use `base::JSONReader::ReadDict()`

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Pass-by-Value for Sink Parameters (Google Style)
summary: Per Google C++ Style Guide, use pass-by-value for parameters that will be moved into the callee
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - rvalue reference parameter
void SetName(std::string&& name) { name_ = std::move(name); }
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - pass by value
void SetName(std::string name) { name_ = std::move(name); }

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Annotate Obsolete Pref Migration Entries with Dates
summary: When adding preference migration code that removes deprecated prefs, annotate the entry with the date it was added.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - no context for when this was added
profile_prefs->ClearPref(kOldFeaturePref);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - annotated with date
profile_prefs->ClearPref(kOldFeaturePref);  // Added 2025-01 (safe to remove after ~3 releases)

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::FindOrNull()` for Map Lookups
summary: Use `base::FindOrNull()` instead of the manual find-and-check-end pattern for map lookups.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
return base::FindOrNull(metric_configs_, metric_name);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::Extend` for Appending Ranges to Vectors
summary: Use `base::Extend(target, source)` instead of manual `insert(end, begin, end)` for appending one collection to another.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
base::Extend(accelerator_list, base::span(kBraveAcceleratorMap));

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::test::ParseJson` and `base::ExpectDict*` in Tests
summary: Use `base::test::ParseJson()` for parsing JSON in tests, and `base::test::*` utilities from `base/test/values_test_util.h` for asserting dict contents.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `kOsAll` for Cross-Platform Feature Flags
summary: When registering feature flags in `about_flags.cc` that should be available on all platforms, use `kOsAll`
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - listing platforms individually
{"brave-my-feature", ..., kOsDesktop | kOsAndroid}
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - use kOsAll
{"brave-my-feature", ..., kOsAll}

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Workaround Code Must Have Tracking Issues
summary: Any temporary workaround or hack code must reference a tracking issue with a `TODO(https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/<id>)` comment

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use Named Constants for JSON Property Keys
summary: When accessing JSON object properties in C++, define named constants for the key strings

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Never Return `std::string_view` from Functions That Build Strings
summary: Do not return `std::string_view` from a function that constructs or concatenates a string internally.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Prefer `constexpr int` Over Single-Value Enums
summary: When a constant is just a single numeric value, use `constexpr int` rather than creating a single-value enum.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - enum for a single value
enum { kBravePolicySource = 10 };
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - constexpr int
constexpr int kBravePolicySource = 10;

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::FilePath` for File Path Parameters
summary: Parameters representing file system paths should use `base::FilePath` instead of `std::string`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - generic string for a path
std::string GetProfileId(const std::string& profile_path);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - domain-specific type
std::string GetProfileId(const base::FilePath& profile_path);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Explicitly Assign Enum Values When Conditionally Compiling Out Members
summary: When conditionally compiling out enum values behind a build flag, explicitly assign numeric values to remaining members.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Name All Function Parameters in Header Declarations
summary: Always name function parameters in header declarations, especially when types alone are ambiguous.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Struct Members: No Trailing Underscores
summary: Plain struct members should not have trailing underscores.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Introduce New Uses of Deprecated APIs
summary: When an API is marked deprecated, never introduce new uses.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - base::Hash deprecated for 6+ years
uint32_t hash = base::Hash(str);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - use the recommended replacement
uint32_t hash = base::FastHash(base::as_byte_span(str));

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Default-Initialize POD-Type Members in Headers
summary: Plain old data (POD) type members in structs and classes declared in headers must have explicit default initialization.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Prefer `std::string_view` Over `const char*` for Parameters
summary: Use `std::string_view` instead of `const char*` for function parameters that accept string data.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
std::string_view GetDomain(const char* env_from_switch);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
std::string_view GetDomain(std::string_view env_from_switch);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: ⚠️ `std::string_view` Class Members — Know When They're Safe
summary: Storing `std::string_view` as a class member is dangerous in general
body:
**Storing `std::string_view` as a class member is dangerous in general** because
the referenced data must outlive the object. However, there are well-established
safe patterns:

**NEVER flag these safe `std::string_view` member patterns as lifetime bugs:**

- Members initialized from `inline constexpr char[]` constants (e.g., pref keys
  like `kMyPrefName`), `kFeatureName` string literals, or other compile-time
  string constants with static storage duration
- Members initialized from string literals directly (`"some_string"`)
- Members in short-lived stack objects where the caller's string clearly
  outlives the object

**Dangerous — flag these:**

- Members initialized from `std::string` temporaries or function return values
- Members in long-lived objects (singletons, services) initialized from
  non-static strings
- Members where the constructor accepts `std::string_view` and the caller might
  pass a temporary

```cpp
// ✅ SAFE - pref keys are inline constexpr with static lifetime
class MyMetrics {
  std::string_view histogram_name_;  // initialized from kHistogramName
  std::string_view pref_path_;       // initialized from prefs::kMyPref
};

// ❌ DANGEROUS - caller could pass a temporary
class Config {
  std::string_view name_;  // who owns the underlying string?
  Config(std::string_view name) : name_(name) {}  // dangles if temp passed
};
```

**When reviewing:** Check what the `string_view` member is actually initialized
from before flagging. Pref key constants and string literals have static
lifetime and are safe.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `base::circular_deque` Over `std::deque`
summary: Always use `base::circular_deque` (or `base::queue`/`base::stack`) instead of `std::deque` (or `std::queue`/`std::stack`).

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `size_t` for Sizes, Counts, and Indices
summary: Use `size_t` for object sizes, allocation sizes, element counts, array offsets, and vector indices.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use Transparent Comparisons for `base::flat_map` String Lookups
summary: `base::flat_map` and `base::flat_set` support transparent comparisons, enabling lookups with `std::string_view` or `const char*` without constructing temporary `std::string` objects.
body:
**`base::flat_map` and `base::flat_set` support transparent comparisons,
enabling lookups with `std::string_view` or `const char*` without constructing
temporary `std::string` objects.** This avoids unnecessary heap allocations on
lookups.

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - operator[] constructs a temporary std::string
base::flat_map<std::string, int> map;
int val = map["key"];  // temporary std::string("key") created

// ✅ CORRECT - find() uses transparent comparison, no temporary
base::flat_map<std::string, int> map;
auto it = map.find("key");  // no temporary string created
```

For `base::flat_set` of `std::unique_ptr`, use `base::UniquePtrComparator` for
transparent lookups by raw pointer. See
[Chromium container guidelines](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/base/containers/README.md).

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Don't Rely on Implicit `const char*` → `string_view` for Non-Null-Terminated Data
summary: When constructing `std::string_view` from a byte buffer or `reinterpret_cast`'d pointer, always pass the size explicitly.

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: String Usage in Rust/C++ FFI
summary: Pick FFI string types by data flow (borrow vs. own) and payload size (standard vs. large).
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - bridge type leaks into idiomatic Rust code
fn is_valid_key(key: &CxxString) -> bool;

// ❌ WRONG - container copy through rust::String layout
fn produce_payload() -> String;

// ❌ WRONG - forces deep copy of large buffer
fn ingest(blob: String);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - pointer move, zero-copy
fn produce_payload() -> Box<Vec<u8>>;

// ✅ CORRECT - C++ deep-copies at the call site
fn store_name(name: String);

// ✅ CORRECT - zero-copy pointer move
fn ingest(blob: UniquePtr<CxxString>);

docTitle: C++ API Usage, Containers & Type Safety
title: Use `std::u16string` for 16-Bit Strings, Not `std::wstring`
summary: Chromium uses UTF-16 extensively — use `std::u16string` and `char16_t*`, and declare UTF-16 literals with the `u"..."` prefix.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - wstring in cross-platform code
std::wstring title = L"Brave";

// ❌ WRONG - byte escapes in a UTF-16 literal
std::u16string bullet = u"\xe2\x80\xa2";
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
std::u16string title = u"Brave";

title: Add `#endif` Comments for Clarity
summary: Add `#endif` comments to clarify what each `#endif` is closing.
body:
**Add `#endif` comments to clarify what each `#endif` is closing.** See the
"Refined Rule: `#endif` Comments Based on Block Length" section below for
specific guidance on when to include vs omit these comments.

```cpp
#if BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_SPELLCHECK)
#include "components/spellcheck/common/spellcheck_features.h"
#endif  // BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_SPELLCHECK)
```

title: Guard an Include Only When the Header Is Conditionally Available
summary: Move an `#include` inside a `#if BUILDFLAG(...)` block only when the header itself is conditionally available

title: Merge Consecutive Identical BUILDFLAG Blocks
summary: When multiple consecutive code regions use the same `#if BUILDFLAG(...)` condition, merge them into a single guard block.

title: Refined Rule: `#endif` Comments Based on Block Length
summary: Clarification of the `#endif` comment rule:
body:
**Clarification of the `#endif` comment rule:**

- **Always add** for blocks > 3 lines
- **Always add** when inside nested `#if` blocks
- **Always add** when surrounding code already uses them (consistency)
- **Can omit** for short (1-2 line), unambiguous blocks

title: Add `static_assert` in Public Headers for Build Flag Guards
summary: When introducing a build flag for a component, add `static_assert` in public-facing headers

title: Forward Declarations Don't Need `BUILDFLAG` Guards
summary: Only `#include` directives and actual usages need to be wrapped in `#if BUILDFLAG(...)` guards.

title: Don't Include Buildflag Headers in Conditionally-Compiled Files
summary: If a file is only compiled when a buildflag is enabled (guarded by `if(enable_feature)` in BUILD.gn), that file should not `#include` the buildflag header just to re-check the enable/disable flag with `#if BUILDFLAG(...)`.
body:
**If a file is only compiled when a buildflag is enabled (guarded by
`if(enable_feature)` in BUILD.gn), that file should not `#include` the buildflag
header just to re-check the enable/disable flag with `#if BUILDFLAG(...)`.** The
file is never compiled when the flag is disabled, so re-checking that same flag
inside it is redundant and misleading.

This applies only to the enable/disable flag that already gates the file.
Buildflags also carry other GN-passed parameters (keys, URLs, numeric limits,
etc.), and reading those values is perfectly valid — in that case including the
buildflag header is expected, not redundant.

```cpp
// In brave/components/foo/foo_impl.cc
// (only in sources when enable_foo = true in BUILD.gn)

// ❌ WRONG - redundant buildflag include and guard
#include "brave/components/foo/common/buildflags/buildflags.h"

#if BUILDFLAG(ENABLE_FOO)
void DoFoo() { ... }
#endif

// ✅ CORRECT - file is already conditionally compiled, no guard needed
void DoFoo() { ... }
```

Note: Public headers may still benefit from a `static_assert(BUILDFLAG(...))` as
a safety net against accidental inclusion (see BS-049). This rule applies to
implementation files and internal headers that are strictly behind the BUILD.gn
guard.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - file is already conditionally compiled, no guard needed
void DoFoo() { ... }

title: Prefer unique_ptr Over new/delete
summary: Avoid manual new/delete. Use unique_ptr, stack variables, or member initializer lists.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - use unique_ptr or member initializer list
: predictor_(std::make_unique<BandwidthSavingsPredictor>(extractor))

title: Don't Take Ownership of Unowned Resources
summary: If a class doesn't own a resource, don't create ownership wrappers for it. This is a common source of crashes (see also architecture.md on shared_ptr misuse).
body:
If a class doesn't own a resource, don't create ownership wrappers for it. This
is a common source of crashes (see also architecture.md on shared_ptr misuse).

title: `shared_ptr` Is Banned in Chromium Code
summary: Do not use `std::shared_ptr` - it is on the Chromium banned features list.
body:
**Do not use `std::shared_ptr` - it is on the Chromium banned features list.**
Use `base::RefCounted` / `scoped_refptr` when shared ownership is truly needed,
or restructure to use unique ownership.

title: Invalidate WeakPtrs During Teardown
summary: Call `weak_factory_.InvalidateWeakPtrs()` at the start of shutdown/cleanup.

title: Always Check WeakPtr Validity Before Use
summary: Always check a `base::WeakPtr` is valid before dereferencing, especially after async operations.

title: Prefer `base::WeakPtrFactory` Over `SupportsWeakPtr`
summary: Use `base::WeakPtrFactory<T>` as a member rather than inheriting from `base::SupportsWeakPtr<T>`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
class MyClass : public base::SupportsWeakPtr<MyClass> {};

title: WeakPtr - Bind to Member Function, Not Lambda Capture
summary: When using WeakPtr with async callbacks, bind directly to a member function.

title: Never Use `base::Unretained` with Thread Pool
summary: Never use `base::Unretained` when posting work to thread pools.

title: Use `base::Unretained(this)` for Self-Owned Timer Callbacks
summary: When a class owns a `base::RepeatingTimer` or `base::OneShotTimer`, prefer `base::Unretained(this)`.
body:
**When a class owns a `base::RepeatingTimer` or `base::OneShotTimer`, prefer
`base::Unretained(this)`.** The timer is destroyed with the class, so it can
only fire while `this` is valid. Using `WeakPtr` adds unnecessary overhead, but
**NEVER report it as a correctness bug.** This is a style preference.

```cpp
// ⚠️ AVOID - unnecessary overhead (but not a bug)
timer_.Start(FROM_HERE, delay,
    base::BindRepeating(&MyClass::OnTimer, weak_factory_.GetWeakPtr()));

// ✅ PREFERRED - timer is owned, so this is always valid when it fires
timer_.Start(FROM_HERE, delay,
    base::BindRepeating(&MyClass::OnTimer, base::Unretained(this)));
```

**Key distinction:** This is the opposite of the "never use Unretained with
thread pool" rule. The difference is ownership: you own the timer, so it cannot
outlive you. If a developer prefers `WeakPtr` for defensive coding, that's a
valid choice — **NEVER insist on changing it.**

title: `base::Unretained(this)` Is Safe with Owned Mojo Endpoints
summary: Using `base::Unretained(this)` in Mojo disconnect handlers and connection error handlers is safe when the class owns the `mojo::Remote`, `mojo::Receiver`, or `mojo::AssociatedRemote`.

title: Place `raw_ptr<>` Members Last in Class Declarations
summary: In class declarations, place unowned `raw_ptr<>` members after owning members

title: Never Bind `std::vector<raw_ptr<T>>` in Callbacks
summary: Never capture `std::vector<raw_ptr<T>>` in async callbacks.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - raw_ptrs may dangle
base::BindOnce(&OnComplete, std::move(raw_ptr_vector));

title: Use `SEQUENCE_CHECKER` Consistently - All Methods or None
summary: If a class is single-threaded, either apply `DCHECK_CALLED_ON_VALID_SEQUENCE` to all methods or remove the sequence checker entirely.
body:
**If a class is single-threaded, either apply `DCHECK_CALLED_ON_VALID_SEQUENCE`
to all methods or remove the sequence checker entirely.** Partial checking is
misleading and makes correct code look unsafe.

title: Clean Up Resources in `KeyedService::Shutdown`
summary: For `KeyedService` implementations, clean up owned resources in `Shutdown()`, not just the destructor.
body:
**For `KeyedService` implementations, clean up owned resources in `Shutdown()`,
not just the destructor.** The service graph has dependencies requiring orderly
teardown.

title: Unsubscribe Observers in `::Shutdown()` Even with `ScopedObservation`
summary: `ScopedObservation` can still lead to use-after-free.

title: Don't Pass `BrowserContext` to Component Services
summary: Component-level services should take specific dependencies (`PrefService*`, `URLLoaderFactory`) rather than `BrowserContext`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
explicit MyFeatureService(content::BrowserContext* context);

title: Add Thread Checks to `base::Bind` Callback Targets
summary: Methods used as targets of `base::BindOnce` / `base::BindRepeating` should include `DCHECK_CALLED_ON_VALID_SEQUENCE` to ensure correct thread.
body:
**Methods used as targets of `base::BindOnce` / `base::BindRepeating` should
include `DCHECK_CALLED_ON_VALID_SEQUENCE` to ensure correct thread.**

title: Use `base::NoDestructor` for Non-Trivial Static Objects
summary: Chromium prohibits global objects with non-trivial destructors.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - global map with non-trivial destructor
static const std::map<std::string, int> kMyLookup = {{"foo", 1}, {"bar", 2}};

title: Consider `base::SequenceBound` for Thread-Isolated Operations
summary: When a class performs blocking or IO operations and needs to be accessed asynchronously from the UI thread, use `base::SequenceBound<T>`.

title: Explicitly Specify `base::TaskPriority` in Thread Pool Tasks
summary: When posting tasks to the thread pool, explicitly specify `base::TaskPriority` and shutdown behavior
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - implicit priority
base::ThreadPool::PostTask(FROM_HERE, {base::MayBlock()}, task);

title: Don't Use Synchronous OSCrypt in New Code
summary: New code must use the async OSCrypt interface, not the legacy synchronous one.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - deprecated sync interface
OSCrypt::EncryptString(plaintext, &ciphertext);

title: Use Delegates Instead of Raw Callbacks for Cross-Layer Dependencies
summary: When a component-level class needs platform-specific behavior, use a delegate pattern with a dedicated delegate class instead of passing raw callbacks.

title: Use `reset_on_disconnect()` for Simple Mojo Cleanup
summary: For simple Mojo remote cleanup on disconnection (just resetting the remote), use `remote.reset_on_disconnect()`
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - built-in reset on disconnect
remote_.reset_on_disconnect();

title: Use `tabs::TabHandle` Over Raw `WebContents*` for Stored References
summary: When storing tab references, prefer `tabs::TabHandle` (integer identifiers) over raw `WebContents*` pointers.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - raw pointer can dangle and point to wrong tab
std::vector<content::WebContents*> tabs_to_close_;

title: Security Review for Unrestricted URL Inputs in Mojom
summary: When creating mojom interfaces that accept URL parameters from less-privileged processes, consider restricting to an allowlist or enum
body:
**When creating mojom interfaces that accept URL parameters from less-privileged
processes, consider restricting to an allowlist or enum** rather than accepting
arbitrary URLs. An unrestricted URL parameter means the renderer can send
requests to any endpoint.

**NEVER request documentation comments about URL validation if the
implementation already validates or filters the URL downstream.** Before
flagging, check whether similar patterns in surrounding code or elsewhere in the
codebase have such comments — if they don't, your suggestion would introduce
inconsistency and unnecessary verbosity.

title: `base::DoNothing()` Doesn't Match `base::FunctionRef` Signatures
summary: `base::DoNothing()` cannot be used where a `base::FunctionRef<void(T&)>` is expected.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - won't compile
service->ForEach(base::DoNothing());  // FunctionRef<void(Item&)>
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - explicit lambda
service->ForEach([](Item&) {});

title: Null-Check Return Values Before Dereferencing
summary: Always null-check return values from methods that can return nullptr before dereferencing, even when the input argument seems valid.

title: Don't Use a Variable After `std::move()`
summary: Never read or use a variable after it has been `std::move()`-d.

title: Don't Pass Smart Pointers by Const Reference
summary: Don't use `const std::unique_ptr<T>&` or `const scoped_refptr<T>&` as function parameters.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - forces callers to heap-allocate
void Process(const std::unique_ptr<Foo>& foo);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - raw pointer decouples ownership from allocation
void Process(Foo* foo);

// ✅ CORRECT - reference when non-null is required
void Process(Foo& foo);

title: Avoid Reference-Counted Objects — Prefer Redesign
summary: Reference-counted objects (`base::RefCounted`/`scoped_refptr`) make ownership and destruction order difficult to reason about, especially with multiple threads.
body:
**Reference-counted objects (`base::RefCounted`/`scoped_refptr`) make ownership
and destruction order difficult to reason about, especially with multiple
threads.** Prefer redesigning to use single ownership (`std::unique_ptr`). See
[Chromium smart pointer guidelines](https://www.chromium.org/developers/smart-pointer-guidelines/).

When refcounting seems necessary:

- Restrict the class to a single thread/sequence
- Use `PostTask()` to proxy calls to the correct thread
- Use `base::BindOnce()` with `WeakPtr` for automatic cancellation on
  destruction

title: Don't Hold Pointers to `base::Value` From PrefService
summary: It is not safe to store a pointer to a `base::Value` (or `base::Value::Dict`, etc.) returned from `PrefService`.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - clone the value for longer-lived usage
base::Value::Dict dict = pref_service->GetDict(kMyPref).Clone();

// ✅ CORRECT - use inline if only needed briefly
if (pref_service->GetDict(kMyPref).FindString("key")) { ... }

title: Declare Members in Reverse Dependency Order for Safe Destruction
summary: C++ destroys class members in reverse declaration order. If one member depends on another (e.g., a map of `string_view` pointing into a `deque<string>`), declare the depended-upon member first so it is destroyed last.

title: Prefer `base::SequenceLocalStorageSlot` Over `thread_local`
summary: For sequence-aware code, use `base::SequenceLocalStorageSlot` instead of `thread_local`.
body:
**For sequence-aware code, use `base::SequenceLocalStorageSlot` instead of
`thread_local`.** It integrates with Chromium's task runner model and avoids the
strict requirements of `thread_local`.

When `thread_local` is truly needed, Chromium requires:

- Type must satisfy `std::is_trivially_destructible_v<T>` (`raw_ptr` is
  excluded)
- Cannot be exported via `COMPONENT_EXPORT`
- Namespace/class scope requires `ABSL_CONST_INIT` annotation
- Cannot be constructed in OOM handlers (POSIX construction may allocate)

If these requirements cannot be met, use `base::ThreadLocalOwnedPointer`
instead. See
[Chromium C++ style guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md).

title: Use `const raw_ref<T>` for Fields That Must Never Be Null; `raw_ptr<T>` Otherwise
summary: Per the [Chromium C++ Style Guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md), class and struct fields should be written `const raw_ref<T>` or `raw_ptr<T>` rather than `T&` or `T*` whenever possible.

title: Don't Bind Unowned View Types into Callbacks
summary: `base::Bind*` already rejects the unsafe raw-pointer and reference cases at compile time (it forces `base::Unretained`, refuses raw pointers to ref-counted types, etc.), but it does _not_ catch non-owning "view" types like `std::string_view` and `base::span<T>`.

title: Flag `base::Unretained` Only When the Callback Can Outlive `this`
summary: `base::Unretained(this)` is safe whenever the bound callback is owned by `this` — directly or through a member that is destroyed with `this` — so the callback cannot run after `this` is gone.
body:
**`base::Unretained(this)` is safe whenever the bound callback is owned by
`this` — directly or through a member that is destroyed with `this` — so the
callback cannot run after `this` is gone.** This is the common, correct pattern;
the only genuinely problematic case is a callback that can outlive `this`.
**NEVER flag the member-owned callbacks below or request a `WeakPtr` replacement
when they cannot outlive `this`.**

Safe — the callback's owner is a member destroyed with `this`:

- A `PrefChangeRegistrar` held as a member (including one observing
  `local_state`) — its destructor unregisters every observer, so the callback
  cannot fire afterwards
- `base::OneShotTimer` / `base::RepeatingTimer` members (see
  [CSM-011](#CSM-011))
- Owned `mojo::Receiver`, `mojo::Remote`, or `mojo::AssociatedRemote`
  disconnect/error handlers (see [CSM-012](#CSM-012))
- A `base::CallbackListSubscription` stored as a member

```cpp
// ✅ SAFE - the registrar is a member destroyed with `this`, so the
// callback cannot fire after `this` is gone.
pref_change_registrar_.Init(prefs_);
pref_change_registrar_.Add(
    kSomePref,
    base::BindRepeating(&MyClass::OnPrefChanged, base::Unretained(this)));
```

Problematic — the callback can outlive `this` (use a `WeakPtr` instead):

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - posted to another sequence; `this` may be freed before it runs
base::ThreadPool::PostTask(
    FROM_HERE, base::BindOnce(&MyClass::DoWork, base::Unretained(this)));
```

Only flag `base::Unretained` when the callback is posted to a thread pool or
another sequence (see [CSM-010](#CSM-010)), stored in a longer-lived object, or
handed to an API whose lifetime is independent of `this`. A linter that flags
every `base::Unretained(this)` produces mostly false positives, since
member-owned callbacks are the dominant, correct usage.

title: Let Pointer Types in Signatures Express Ownership
summary: The pointer type in a parameter or return type is the ownership contract.
body:
**The pointer type in a parameter or return type is the ownership contract.**
Follow the
[Chromium smart pointer guidelines](https://www.chromium.org/developers/smart-pointer-guidelines/)
so callers don't have to read the implementation to learn who frees what.

**Parameters:**

| Declare              | Meaning                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `T*` / `T&`          | No ownership change; caller keeps `t` alive for the call                              |
| `std::unique_ptr<T>` | The function takes ownership                                                          |
| `scoped_refptr<T>`   | The function may take a ref; the caller chooses `std::move(t)` or keeping its own ref |

**A smart pointer is not the default way to move a value.** When the type is
moveable, take it by value — `void Consume(T value)`, called as
`Consume(std::move(t))` — and reach for `std::unique_ptr<T>` only when the type
is not moveable, which is typically the case for polymorphic types held by base
pointer. Much of the `std::unique_ptr<T>` in existing code is historical: before
move semantics it was the only way to hand an object around, and before
`std::optional<T>` it doubled as the way to express "maybe a value".

**Return values:**

| Return                                             | Meaning                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `T*`                                               | If and only if the caller does _not_ take ownership                         |
| `std::unique_ptr<T>` / `scoped_refptr<T>` by value | The implementation is handing off ownership                                 |
| `const scoped_refptr<T>&`                          | The implementation retains ownership; the caller isn't forced to take a ref |

The same caveat applies to returns: for a moveable type, return a plain `T` by
value rather than wrapping it in a smart pointer to hand it back.

**A function must never take ownership of a parameter passed as `T*`.** That is
the single most common violation, and it's invisible at the call site.

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - silently deletes a pointer the caller still owns
void SetDelegate(Delegate* delegate);  // impl does: delegate_.reset(delegate
…
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - silently deletes a pointer the caller still owns
void SetDelegate(Delegate* delegate);  // impl does: delegate_.reset(delegate);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - ownership transfer is visible at every call site
void SetDelegate(std::unique_ptr<Delegate> delegate);

// ✅ CORRECT - borrowing only
void UseDelegate(Delegate* delegate);

body:

arbitrarily use different names in different places for the same thing.

```cpp

C++: IsTorDisabledManaged()
JS:  getTorManaged()

// ✅ CORRECT - consistent naming

summary: Never copy a Chromium file and use Brave's copyright.
body:
**Never copy a Chromium file and use Brave's copyright.** If you copy or derive
from Chromium code, you must include their copyright notice. The original year

summary: New files must use the current year in the copyright header.
body:
**New files must use the current year in the copyright header.** Always
determine the current year from the system date (e.g., `date +%Y`), never from
training data or memory — the training cutoff year is often outdated. Don't
copy-paste old copyright years from other files.

summary: In class declarations, `friend` statements should be placed immediately after the `private:` access specifier,

wrong:

static void InternalHelper() { ... }

summary: Function definitions in `.cc` files should appear in the same order as their declarations in the corresponding `.h` file.

right:

StartPasswordImport();

title: Document Non-Obvious Failure Branches
summary: When a function has multiple early-return failure branches, add a brief comment before each summarizing what it handles.
