summary: Comments explaining what a `base::Feature` does should be placed in the `.cc` file where the feature is defined, not in the `.h` file.

title: Document Upstream Workarounds with Issue Links
summary: When adding a workaround for an upstream Chromium bug:

title: Don't Use Positional Terms in Code Comments
summary: Do not use "above" or "below" in comments to reference other code.

title: Use CHECK for Impossible Conditions
summary: Use `CHECK` (not `DCHECK`) for conditions that should never happen in any build.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - DCHECK for something that should never happen
DCHECK(browser_context);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - CHECK for impossible conditions
CHECK(browser_context);  // should never be null

title: `NOTREACHED`/`CHECK(false)` Only to ensure invariants hold
summary: See first the Chromimum guide on this [CHECK(), DCHECK() and NOTREACHED()](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/styleguide/c++/checks.md) which outlines best practices around them. It also list helpful examples around the usage.
body:
See first the Chromimum guide on this
[CHECK(), DCHECK() and NOTREACHED()](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/styleguide/c++/checks.md)
which outlines best practices around them. It also list helpful examples around
the usage.

**`NOTREACHED`/`CHECK(false)` should only crash the browser for invariants.**
For other cases (like invalid enum values from data processing), prefer
returning `std::optional`/`std::nullopt` or a default value.

**Important:** `NOTREACHED()` is now fatal in all builds and terminates control
flow. The compiler treats code after `NOTREACHED()` as dead code. Do not place
executable statements after it.

**Gradual migration:** When migrating from `DCHECK` to fatal
`NOTREACHED()`/`CHECK()`, you can use `NOTREACHED(base::NotFatalUntil::M140)` or
`CHECK(cond, base::NotFatalUntil::M140)` to gather crash diagnostics before
enforcing fatality. See
[Chromium style guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md).

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - crashes browser for non-security enum mismatch
mojom::AdType ToMojomAdType(const std::string& type) {
  // ...
  NOTREACHED();  // This isn't a security issue!
}

// ✅ CORRECT - return optional for non-security case
std::optional<mojom::AdType> ToMojomAdType(const std::string& type) {
  // ...
  return std::nullopt;  // Caller handles gracefully
}
```

title: Use `CHECK` Only for Invariants Within Code's Control
summary: Use `CHECK` only for conditions fully within the code's control.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - crashes on external data
CHECK(db_value.has_value());  // Data from database!

title: Use Result Codes, Not bool, for Error Reporting
summary: Return result codes (enums) instead of `bool` for operations that can fail.
body:
**Return result codes (enums) instead of `bool` for operations that can fail.**
This allows providing additional error information and is more future-proof.

title: Don't Store Error State - Handle/Log and Store Only Success
summary: When a field can hold either a success or error, handle/log the error immediately and store only the success type.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - storing error variant
base::expected<ChainMetadata, std::string> chain_metadata_;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - handle error at failure point, store only success
std::optional<ChainMetadata> chain_metadata_;

title: Don't Override Empty/No-Op Methods
summary: If you're overriding a virtual method but not implementing any behavior, don't define it at all.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - pointless override
void OnSomethingHappened() override {}
right: // ✅ CORRECT - just don't override it

title: Combine Methods That Are Always Called Together
summary: If two methods are always called in sequence (especially in patches), combine them into a single method.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - single combined method
+PrepareBinaries(params);  // internally calls both

title: Use Observer Pattern for UI Updates
summary: Don't make service-layer queries to update UI directly.

title: Platform-Specific Code Splitting
summary: When a method's implementation is completely different on a platform, split it into a separate file
body:
**When a method's implementation is completely different on a platform, split it
into a separate file** like `my_class_android.cc` rather than filling the main
file with `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)` blocks.

**Always use the buildflags from `build/build_config.h`** — `BUILDFLAG(IS_WIN)`,
`BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)`, `BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC)`, etc. Never test compiler-provided
macros like `WIN32`, `__APPLE__`, or `__linux__`, and never the long-removed
`defined(OS_*)` form. See
[Chromium C++ style guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md).

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - compiler macro
#if defined(WIN32)

// ❌ WRONG - `OS_ANDROID` was replaced by the BUILDFLAG form
#if defined(OS_ANDROID)

// ✅ CORRECT
#include "build/build_config.h"
#if BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)
```

Put platform-specific `#include`s in their own section below the standard
includes, repeating the normal include order within that section. Ordering is
formatting, not review material — per [CS-010](#CS-010), leave it to
`clang-format` and lint. **NEVER flag include order in review.**
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - compiler macro
#if defined(WIN32)

// ❌ WRONG - `OS_ANDROID` was replaced by the BUILDFLAG form
#if defined(OS_ANDROID)

summary: Prefer feature checks over platform checks when the behavior is feature-dependent, not platform-dependent.

title: Consolidate Feature Flag Checks to Entry Points
summary: Don't scatter `CHECK`/`DCHECK` for feature flag status in private helper functions.

title: Don't Use Static Variables for Per-Profile Settings
summary: Never use static variables to store per-profile settings.
body:
**Never use static variables to store per-profile settings.** Static state is
shared across all profiles and will cause incorrect behavior in multi-profile
scenarios. Use `UserData` or profile-attached keyed services instead.

title: Don't Use Environment Variables for Configuration
summary: Configuration should come from GN args, not environment variables.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
std::string api_url = std::getenv("BRAVE_API_URL");
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - GN arg with command line override option
// In BUILD.gn: defines += [ "BRAVE_API_URL=\"$brave_api_url\"" ]

title: Don't Duplicate Enum/Constant Values Across Languages
summary: When values are defined in Mojo, use the generated bindings in C++, Java, and JS.
body:
**When values are defined in Mojo, use the generated bindings in C++, Java, and
JS.** Don't manually duplicate constants - they easily drift out of sync.

title: Don't Use rapidjson
summary: Use base::JSONReader/JSONWriter, not rapidjson.
body:
**Use base::JSONReader/JSONWriter, not rapidjson.** The base libraries are the
standard in Chromium.

title: VLOG Macros Handle Their Own Checks
summary: Don't use `VLOG_IS_ON` before `VLOG` calls.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - VLOG handles it
VLOG(2) << "Some message";

title: VLOG Component Name Should Match Directory
summary: The component name used in VLOG messages should match the component directory name
body:
**The component name used in VLOG messages should match the component directory
name** (e.g., `policy` or `brave/components/brave_policy`).

title: Use `LOG(WARNING)` or `VLOG` Instead of `LOG(ERROR)` for Non-Critical Failures
summary: `LOG(ERROR)` should be reserved for truly unexpected and serious failures.
body:
**`LOG(ERROR)` should be reserved for truly unexpected and serious failures.**
For expected or non-critical failure cases (e.g., a bad user-supplied filter
list, a failed parse of optional data), use `VLOG` for debug info or
`LOG(WARNING)` for noteworthy but non-critical issues.

**NEVER suggest lowering log severity for failures you haven't confirmed are
non-critical.** The developer knows whether a failure is critical for their
service better than a reviewer can infer from the code alone. For example,
failing to load a model file may look non-critical in isolation but could be a
critical failure for the keyed service that depends on it.

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG
LOG(ERROR) << "Failed to parse filter list";

// ✅ CORRECT
VLOG(1) << "Failed to parse filter list";
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
LOG(ERROR) << "Failed to parse filter list";
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
VLOG(1) << "Failed to parse filter list";

// ❌ WRONG - release log noise for non-critical error
LOG(ERROR) << "Failed to parse optional field";
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - debug-only logging
DLOG(ERROR) << "Failed to parse optional field";

summary: When writing code that processes data on the UI thread or performs potentially slow operations, add `SCOPED_UMA_HISTOGRAM_TIMER` to measure performance.

summary: When recording UMA histograms, emit to each histogram from a single location.

summary: Never log sensitive data such as sync seeds, private keys, tokens, or credentials.

// ❌ WRONG
VLOG(1) << "Sync seed: " << sync_seed;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
VLOG(1) << "Sync seed set successfully";

summary: Do not use `public:` labels in struct declarations since struct members are public by default.

wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - truncates to 0 for used < total
int pct = (used / total) * 100;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - preserves precision

summary: When a lambda is complex enough to make surrounding code harder to parse, extract it into a named free function in the anonymous namespace.

summary: Don't use `auto` merely to avoid writing a type name
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - auto hides a short, descriptive type

right:
// ✅ CORRECT - explicit type adds readability
base::TimeDelta elapsed = timer.Elapsed();

summary: Per Chromium C++ dos and donts: "Initialize class members in their declarations, **except where a member's value is explicitly set by every constructor**."

title: Prefer Overloads Over Silently-Ignored Optional Parameters
summary: Don't force callers to provide parameters that are silently ignored.
body:
**Don't force callers to provide parameters that are silently ignored.** Use
function overloads. Similarly, prefer overloads over `std::variant` for distinct
call patterns.

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG - body_value silently ignored for GET/HEAD
void ApiFetch(const std::string& verb, const std::string& url,
              const base::Value& body_value, Callback cb);

// ✅ CORRECT - separate overloads
void ApiFetch(const std::string& url, Callback cb);  // GET
void ApiFetch(const std::string& url, const base::Value& body, Callback cb);  // POST
```

summary: Use `observers_.Notify(&Observer::Method)` instead of manually iterating observer lists.

observers_.Notify(&Observer::OnPoliciesChanged);

summary: When constructing JavaScript from C++ data for injection, use JSON serialization (`base::JSONWriter`) for safe encoding.

summary: In browser tests, use `EvalJs` and `ExecJs` instead of the deprecated `ExecuteScriptAndExtractBool/String/Int` functions.

EXPECT_EQ(true, content::EvalJs(web_contents, "someCheck()"));

Profile* profile = static_cast<Profile*>(browser_context);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
Profile* profile = Profile::FromBrowserContext(browser_context);

summary: Declare time constants as `constexpr base::TimeDelta` rather than just `const`.
wrong:

const base::TimeDelta kAnimationDuration = base::Milliseconds(200);
right:

constexpr base::TimeDelta kAnimationDuration = base::Milliseconds(200);

title: Clean Up All Dead Code When Removing Features
summary: When removing a feature flag, model, or script, also remove all associated dead code:
body:
**When removing a feature flag, model, or script, also remove all associated
dead code:** unused helper functions, orphaned UI strings from `.grdp` files,
related constants, and utility functions that were only referenced by the
removed code. Leaving dead code behind creates maintenance burden and confusion.

title: Avoid Multiple Inheritance Beyond Interfaces
summary: Multiple inheritance is permitted in Chromium but discouraged beyond interface-style patterns.
body:
**Multiple inheritance is permitted in Chromium but discouraged beyond
interface-style patterns.** Prefer composition over deep multiple inheritance
hierarchies. If you inherit from multiple concrete classes, explore whether
composition achieves the same goal more cleanly. See
[Chromium C++ style guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md).

title: Use `DVLOG(1)` for Retained Logging, `ScopedCrashKeyString` for Crash Diagnostics
summary: Per the Chromium style guide, remove all logging before check-in.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - LOG in production for diagnostics
LOG(ERROR) << "Unexpected state: " << state;
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - DVLOG for retained debug logging
DVLOG(1) << "Processing state: " << state;

title: Use `*.mojom-forward.h` in Headers When Only Forward Declarations Are Needed
summary: When a header only references mojom types as pointers, references, or function parameters, include the auto-generated `*.mojom-forward.h` instead of the full `*.mojom.h` bindings.

title: Use Security Origins (Not URLs) for Security Decisions on Sites
summary: When extending or limiting capabilities for a site, decide from `url::Origin` / `SecurityOrigin` — never from a raw `GURL`.
body:
**When extending or limiting capabilities for a site, decide from `url::Origin`
/ `SecurityOrigin` — never from a raw `GURL`.** Tie the decision to the exact
`RenderFrameHost` under consideration, and read its origin with
`GetLastCommittedOrigin()`:

```cpp
// ✅ CORRECT - origin of the frame you are deciding about
const url::Origin& origin = render_frame_host->GetLastCommittedOrigin();
```

Converting a `GURL` to an origin is often **not** the origin you expect. See
Chromium's
[origin-vs-url guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/docs/security/origin-vs-url.md)
for the gotchas.

```cpp
// ⚠️ DANGEROUS - GURL → origin is frequently the wrong origin
url::Origin::Create(url);
url::SchemeHostPort(url);
```

If not always, a decision is made on the render frame or the render process (if
the render frame is null; possible for `WebSockets`, `WebTransport`) which is
either making a n/w request or a request to access some browser functionality.
There are generally three scenarios to keep in mind. Starting from
`GetLastCommittedOrigin()` or the `SecurityOrigin`, then apply the extra rules
for these scenarios.

### Frames with non-opaque origins

The usual case: the frame has a tuple origin such as
`https://www.example.com:8080`. Use that origin (or `SecurityOrigin`) directly.

### Frames with opaque origins

Assigned to `file://`, `data:`, and sandboxed frames (`<iframe sandbox>`).
Querying can yield a **null** origin, so there is often little to key a policy
on. A frame with an opaque origin could have both a `null` security origin, and
a "tuple origin" (e.g., https://www.example.com:8080).

These frames already run with limited capabilities — **default to restricted**.
If a decision is still required:

- **Network request:** use the request's `initiator_origin`. See this
  [example change](https://github.com/brave/brave-core/pull/38539/changes#diff-6b02a30e91fdb3e3be80924c66018e9e434a29122f9f6846e2d6f043a05a9c69R84).
- **Otherwise:** If applicable, walk up to the nearest ancestor frame with a
  non-opaque origin and use that. **Important!** Always verify whether that
  non-opaque origin is what was reuqired to base the decisions on.

### Frames with inherited origins

`blob:`, `about:blank`, and `about:srcdoc` **inherit** the embedder frame's
origin. `GetLastCommittedOrigin()` on that `RenderFrameHost` therefore returns
the embedder's origin — which is the origin you should use.

[brave-browser#56048](https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/is
…

title: Don't Use `#pragma once` — Use `#include` Guards
summary: Every header needs a standard `#include` guard; `#pragma once` is not allowed.
body:
**Every header needs a standard `#include` guard; `#pragma once` is not
allowed.** It was historically unsupported on some platforms and doesn't
outperform guards. The guard name is the full path from the source root,
uppercased with `/` and `.` replaced by `_`, plus a trailing `_`. See
[Chromium C++ style guide](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/styleguide/c++/c++.md).

```cpp
// ❌ WRONG
#pragma once

// ✅ CORRECT - brave/components/foo/bar.h
#ifndef BRAVE_COMPONENTS_FOO_BAR_H_
#define BRAVE_COMPONENTS_FOO_BAR_H_

...

#endif  // BRAVE_COMPONENTS_FOO_BAR_H_
```

// ❌ WRONG
#pragma once
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - brave/components/foo/bar.h
#ifndef BRAVE_COMPONENTS_FOO_BAR_H_

...

#endif  // BRAVE_COMPONENTS_FOO_BAR_H_

summary: Always brace the body of an `if`/`else`/`for`/`while`, even a single statement.

title: Use the Right Crash/Diagnostic Primitive
summary: `CHECK`/`NOTREACHED` are for invariants. Reach for a different primitive when that isn't what you mean.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - crashing the browser to report a condition you're still diagnosing
CHECK(entry_was_found);
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - unconditional CHECK
CHECK(profile);

title: Update Documentation Alongside Code Changes
summary: Documentation changes must accompany code modifications in the same changelist.
body:
**Documentation changes must accompany code modifications in the same
changelist.** Don't create separate CLs for documentation updates — they tend to
get forgotten or lose context. Updating docs in the same CL ensures accuracy and
provides reviewers with context about the changes being made.

```
# ❌ WRONG - code change in one CL, docs "later"
CL 1: Refactor RewardsService API
CL 2: (never created) Update RewardsService docs

# ✅ CORRECT - docs updated in the same CL
CL 1: Refactor RewardsService API + update README and method docs
```

CL 2: (never created) Update RewardsService docs
right:

title: Delete Dead Documentation
summary: Remove outdated documentation rather than letting it rot.

title: Method Documentation Should Describe the Contract
summary: Method API documentation should describe the contract: behavior, parameters, return values, gotchas, restrictions, and exceptions.

title: README.md Files Should Orient New Readers
summary: Each major directory should have a README.md that orients new developers.
body:
**Each major directory should have a README.md that orients new developers.** A
good README identifies:

- The purpose of the directory
- Key files and their roles
- How to use the main APIs
- Who maintains the code (team or component)

Start with the simplest use case and build up to advanced usage.

```markdown
# ❌ WRONG - no README, or an empty one

(nothing)

# ✅ CORRECT - orienting README

# Brave Rewards Browser Integration

This directory contains the browser-layer integration for Brave Rewards.

```
wrong:
# ❌ WRONG - no README, or an empty one

(nothing)
right:
# ✅ CORRECT - orienting README

summary: A small amount of accurate, up-to-date documentation is more valuable than extensive documentation in poor condition.
body:
**A small amount of accurate, up-to-date documentation is more valuable than
extensive documentation in poor condition.** Treat documentation like a bonsai
tree — alive but frequently trimmed.

- Don't write docs you won't maintain
- Remove sections that nobody reads or updates
- Focus on the docs that save the most developer time

single integrated story that exercises multiple closely-coupled components
together (e.g., a panel story that covers the full panel with all
sub-components) is sufficient — individual per-component stories are not always
necessary. **NEVER insist on additional stories if the developer considers
existing story coverage adequate.** This is a preference, not a requirement.

title: Avoid Unnecessary `waitFor` in React Tests
summary: In React component tests, if you are using `rerender` to trigger updates, `waitFor` should not be needed
body:
**In React component tests, if you are using `rerender` to trigger updates,
`waitFor` should not be needed** since `rerender` is synchronous. Similarly,
wrapping DOM mutations in `act()` applies pending React updates. Using `waitFor`
unnecessarily makes tests slower and can mask timing-related bugs.

title: Avoid Global State Assumptions for Component-Scoped Operations
summary: When a function accesses global state (like `window.getSelection()`), consider what happens if multiple instances of the component exist on the page.
body:
**When a function accesses global state (like `window.getSelection()`), consider
what happens if multiple instances of the component exist on the page.** If the
function is component-scoped, pass a ref to the specific component instance
instead of relying on global state.

title: ⚠️ Beware `||=` Short-Circuit When Replacing `|=`
summary: Never replace `|=` with `||=` when the right-hand side has side effects.
body:
**Never replace `|=` with `||=` when the right-hand side has side effects.** The
`||=` operator short-circuits: once the left side is truthy, the right side is
never evaluated. If the right side calls a function with side effects, those
effects will be silently skipped.

```typescript
// ❌ WRONG - fn() won't be called once isDirty is true
isDirty ||= updateFileTimestamps(file)

// ❌ ALSO WRONG - fn() skipped when isDirty is already true
isDirty = isDirty || updateFileTimestamps(file)

// ✅ CORRECT - function always executes, result accumulated
isDirty = updateFileTimestamps(file) || isDirty
```

Place the side-effecting call on the LEFT side of `||` to guarantee it always
runs.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - fn() won't be called once isDirty is true
isDirty ||= updateFileTimestamps(file)

// ❌ ALSO WRONG - fn() skipped when isDirty is already true
isDirty = isDirty || updateFileTimestamps(file)
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - function always executes, result accumulated
isDirty = updateFileTimestamps(file) || isDirty

title: Don't Replace Hardcoded Initial CSS With Design Tokens That Load Asynchronously
summary: In WebUI HTML files, keep hardcoded initial background/foreground colors for the page body or root container.
body:
**In WebUI HTML files, keep hardcoded initial background/foreground colors for
the page body or root container.** Design tokens like
`var(--leo-color-container-background)` are loaded asynchronously via JavaScript
— replacing the hardcoded value causes a visible flash of unstyled content
(FOUC) while the token loads.

```html
<!-- ❌ WRONG - Nala token isn't available yet at initial paint -->
<style>
  body {
    background: var(--leo-color-container-background);
  }
</style>

<!-- ✅ CORRECT - hardcoded value matches the token's resolved value, avoids FOUC -->
<style>
  body {
    background: #111114;
  }
</style>
```

Once the page's JavaScript loads and Leo tokens are initialized, the themed
value takes over naturally. The hardcoded value is only visible during the brief
initial paint.
wrong:
<!-- ❌ WRONG - Nala token isn't available yet at initial paint -->
<style>
  body {
    background: var(--leo-color-container-background);
  }
</style>
right:
<!-- ✅ CORRECT - hardcoded value matches the token's resolved value, avoids FOUC -->
<style>
  body {
    background: #111114;
  }
</style>

title: Avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` for External Content
summary: Do not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to render HTML from external or untrusted sources.
body:
**Do not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to render HTML from external or untrusted
sources.** Instead, parse the data and render known safe elements using React
components. If raw HTML rendering is unavoidable, sanitize it first and request
a security review.

title: Clean Up Async Operations in React `useEffect`
summary: Async operations started in `useEffect` must be properly cleaned up to prevent state updates on unmounted components.

summary: Always capture `[weak self]` in closures that outlive the current scope

title: Use `@Observable` Macro, Not `ObservableObject`
summary: Prefer the `@Observable` macro (Observation framework) over `ObservableObject` (Combine).

summary: Mark methods and types that perform UI work as `@MainActor`

title: Use `#available` Compiler Checks
summary: Use `#available` for API availability checks, not manual version comparisons.

title: Prefer Swift Idioms for Concise Code
summary: Use Swift-native patterns instead of verbose alternatives:
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG
let newest = items.sorted(by: { $0.date > $1.date }).first
right:
// ✅ CORRECT
guard let a = optionalA, let b = optionalB else { return }

title: Use `Set` for Membership Testing
summary: Use `Set` instead of `Array` when the primary operation is membership testing (`contains`).

title: Use `public` Not `open` Unless Subclassing Is Required
summary: Default to `public` access control. Only use `open` when external modules need to subclass or override.
body:
**Default to `public` access control. Only use `open` when external modules need
to subclass or override.** Using `open` unnecessarily exposes implementation
details.

title: Prefer Convenience Initializers on Enums Over Static Factory Methods
summary: Use convenience initializers on enums instead of static factory methods.

title: No Default Values for Required Init Parameters
summary: Don't provide default values for parameters that callers should always explicitly specify.
body:
**Don't provide default values for parameters that callers should always
explicitly specify.** This prevents accidental use of incorrect defaults.

title: Use `let` Over `var` for Single-Assignment Properties
summary: Use `let` for properties that are assigned once and never mutated.
body:
**Use `let` for properties that are assigned once and never mutated.** The
compiler enforces immutability, preventing accidental reassignment.

**Exception: NEVER flag `var` properties in Swift structs under this rule.**
Structs control mutability at the usage site via `let`/`var`:

```swift
struct Item {
  var name: String  // OK — mutability controlled by usage
}

let itemOne = Item(name: "...") // itemOne.name is immutable
var itemTwo = Item(name: "...") // itemTwo.name is mutable
```

title: Avoid Implicitly Unwrapped Optionals for viewDidLoad Properties
summary: Do not use implicitly unwrapped optionals (`!`) for properties initialized in `viewDidLoad`.
body:
**Do not use implicitly unwrapped optionals (`!`) for properties initialized in
`viewDidLoad`.** Use lazy properties, optional types with safe unwrapping, or
initialize in the initializer.

**Use `lazy var` only when** you need to defer creation to avoid work at init
time, or when the initializer requires `self`.

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - crash risk if accessed before viewDidLoad
var tableView: UITableView!

// ✅ CORRECT - lazy initialization (defers creation, can reference self)
lazy var tableView = UITableView()
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - crash risk if accessed before viewDidLoad
var tableView: UITableView!
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - lazy initialization (defers creation, can reference self)
lazy var tableView = UITableView()

title: Use `withTaskCancellationHandler` When Bridging Callbacks to Async
summary: When wrapping callback-based APIs with `withCheckedContinuation`, use `withTaskCancellationHandler` to propagate cancellation properly.

title: Always Call Completion Handlers on All Code Paths
summary: When a function accepts a completion handler, always call it on every code path — including error and early-return paths.

title: Use `evaluateSafeJavaScript` Instead of Raw JS Evaluation
summary: Use the `evaluateSafeJavaScript` wrapper instead of calling `callAsyncJavaScript` or `evaluateJavaScript` directly.
body:
**Use the `evaluateSafeJavaScript` wrapper instead of calling
`callAsyncJavaScript` or `evaluateJavaScript` directly.** The wrapper provides
proper error handling and security checks.

title: Model Error States as Swift `Error` Types
summary: Use Swift `Error` enums/structs for error representation, not integer error codes.

title: Delegate Methods Should Take Non-Optional Parameters
summary: Delegate method parameters should be non-optional.
body:
**Delegate method parameters should be non-optional.** The delegate should not
need to handle nil values from the delegating object.

title: Use `_ = variable` to Silence "Wrote But Not Read" Warnings
summary: When a variable is intentionally unused (e.g., the result of a side-effecting function), assign it to `_` explicitly.
body:
**When a variable is intentionally unused (e.g., the result of a side-effecting
function), assign it to `_` explicitly.** This signals intent to future readers
and silences compiler warnings.

title: Use `.clipShape` Instead of Deprecated `.cornerRadius()`
summary: Use `.clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius:))` instead of the deprecated `.cornerRadius()` modifier.
body:
**Use `.clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius:))` instead of the deprecated
`.cornerRadius()` modifier.**

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - deprecated modifier
Text("Hello")
  .cornerRadius(8)

// ✅ CORRECT - modern API
Text("Hello")
  .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 8))
```

title: Use `.background(_:in:)` With Shape Parameter
summary: Use the `.background(_:in:)` modifier with a shape parameter instead of layering `.background()` with `.clipShape()`.
body:
**Use the `.background(_:in:)` modifier with a shape parameter instead of
layering `.background()` with `.clipShape()`.**

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - separate background and clip
Text("Hello")
  .background(Color.blue)
  .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8))

// ✅ CORRECT - combined
Text("Hello")
  .background(.blue, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 8))
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - separate background and clip
Text("Hello")
  .background(Color.blue)
  .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8))

title: Use Stack Spacing Instead of Individual Padding
summary: Use the `spacing` parameter on `VStack`/`HStack` instead of adding padding to each child element.

title: Extract Inline SwiftUI Blocks Into Named Views
summary: When an inline SwiftUI view builder block exceeds a few lines, extract it into a named `View` struct or computed property.
body:
**When an inline SwiftUI view builder block exceeds a few lines, extract it into
a named `View` struct or computed property.** This improves readability and
enables reuse.

title: Use `UIHostingConfiguration` for SwiftUI in UITableViewCell
summary: When using SwiftUI views inside `UITableViewCell` or `UICollectionViewCell`, use `UIHostingConfiguration` instead of manually embedding a `UIHostingController`.

title: Never Modify Constraints in `layoutSubviews`
summary: Do not create or modify Auto Layout constraints inside `layoutSubviews`.

title: Use `setNeedsUpdateConstraints()` for Constraint Changes
summary: When constraints need to change, call `setNeedsUpdateConstraints()`, not `setNeedsLayout()` + `layoutIfNeeded()`.
body:
**When constraints need to change, call `setNeedsUpdateConstraints()`, not
`setNeedsLayout()` + `layoutIfNeeded()`.** The constraint system handles layout
invalidation.

title: Use `UIView.keyboardLayoutGuide` Instead of Manual Keyboard Height
summary: Use `UIView.keyboardLayoutGuide` for keyboard-responsive layouts instead of manually observing keyboard notifications and adjusting insets.
body:
**Use `UIView.keyboardLayoutGuide` for keyboard-responsive layouts instead of
manually observing keyboard notifications and adjusting insets.**

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - manual keyboard observation
NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(self,
  selector: #selector(keyboardWillShow),
  name: UIResponder.keyboardWillShowNotification, object: nil)

// ✅ CORRECT - keyboardLayoutGuide
bottomConstraint = view.bottomAnchor.constraint(
  equalTo: view.keyboardLayoutGuide.topAnchor)
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - manual keyboard observation
NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(self,
  selector: #selector(keyboardWillShow),
  name: UIResponder.keyboardWillShowNotification, object: nil)

title: Use Brave Design System Colors
summary: Use `UIColor(braveSystemName:)` for colors, not hard-coded values.
body:
**Use `UIColor(braveSystemName:)` for colors, not hard-coded values.** This
ensures consistency with the Brave design system and proper dark mode support.

Using system colors is acceptable in settings-like screens where we expect to
match the default styling of iOS.

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - hard-coded color
view.backgroundColor = UIColor(red: 0.2, green: 0.4, blue: 0.8, alpha: 1)

// ✅ CORRECT - design system color
view.backgroundColor = UIColor(braveSystemName: .primary20)
```

// ❌ WRONG - hard-coded color
view.backgroundColor = UIColor(red: 0.2, green: 0.4, blue: 0.8, alpha: 1)
right:

title: Keep Tab Observer and Policy Decider Thin
summary: Do not add feature-specific business logic directly in `BVC+TabObserver.swift` or `BVC+TabPolicyDecider.swift`.
body:
**Do not add feature-specific business logic directly in `BVC+TabObserver.swift`
or `BVC+TabPolicyDecider.swift`.** These files should only contain thin
delegation. Feature-specific logic belongs in `Tab` helpers.

title: Set Properties Before Dependent Setup in `viewDidLoad`
summary: In `viewDidLoad`, set properties before calling setup methods that depend on them.

title: Wrap ObjC Headers With Nullability Annotations
summary: All Objective-C headers should use `NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_BEGIN`/`NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_END` and explicitly annotate nullable parameters.

title: Mark Static-Only ObjC Classes With `NS_UNAVAILABLE` Init
summary: For Objective-C classes that should not be instantiated (only class methods), mark `init` as `NS_UNAVAILABLE`.

title: `OBJC_EXPORT` Goes on Headers Only
summary: `OBJC_EXPORT` should only appear on the header declaration, not the implementation.
body:
**`OBJC_EXPORT` should only appear on the header declaration, not the
implementation.**

title: Use `NS_SWIFT_NAME` to Control Swift Method Naming
summary: Use `NS_SWIFT_NAME` on Objective-C APIs to provide idiomatic Swift names.
body:
**Use `NS_SWIFT_NAME` on Objective-C APIs to provide idiomatic Swift names.**
This is especially important for factory methods and methods with C-style
naming.

title: Use `isEqualToString:` for NSString Comparison
summary: Never use `==` or `!=` for `NSString` comparison — use `isEqualToString:`.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - pointer comparison
if (string == @"expected") { ... }
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - value comparison
if ([string isEqualToString:@"expected"]) { ... }

title: Use camelCase for Obj-C Variable Names Inside Obj-C Classes/Types
summary: Objective-C variable naming must use camelCase inside Obj-C classes and types.
body:
**Objective-C variable naming must use camelCase inside Obj-C classes and
types.** When Obj-C types are used inside C++ classes, follow C++ snake_case
conventions instead.

title: Weak/Strong Dance in Posted Tasks
summary: When posting tasks from Objective-C++ that capture `self`, pass `weakSelf` as a closure parameter rather than capturing it directly.

title: Ensure ObjC Collection Mutability Correctness
summary: Use `copy` for immutable and `mutableCopy` for mutable collections.
body:
**Use `copy` for immutable and `mutableCopy` for mutable collections.** Passing
a mutable collection where an immutable one is expected (or vice versa) leads to
subtle bugs.

title: No Singletons — Use Dependency Injection
summary: Do not use singletons for service access.

title: Tab Helpers Must Use `TabDataValues` Extension Pattern
summary: Tab-associated data should use the `TabDataValues` extension pattern, not stored properties or associated objects.
body:
**Tab-associated data should use the `TabDataValues` extension pattern, not
stored properties or associated objects.** This ensures proper lifecycle
management.

title: Do Not Add Feature Data to `TabState`
summary: Do not add feature-related data directly to `TabState`.
body:
**Do not add feature-related data directly to `TabState`.** Instead, use a Tab
Helper with `TabDataValues` to store feature-specific state. `TabState` should
remain a minimal model representing core tab state.

title: View Model Types Must Not Import SDK Singletons
summary: View models must not import or reference SDK singletons directly.
body:
**View models must not import or reference SDK singletons directly.** Pass SDK
dependencies through the initializer for testability.

title: Bind ProfileIOS Directly, Avoid `getLastUsedProfile`
summary: Pass `ProfileIOS` explicitly into closures and initializers.
body:
**Pass `ProfileIOS` explicitly into closures and initializers.** Do not call
`getLastUsedProfile` at point of use — the last-used profile can change.

title: Feature Flag Checks Gate Registration, Not Runtime
summary: Feature flag checks should gate handler/observer registration, not runtime checks inside the handler.

title: Feature-Specific Logic Does Not Belong in Generic Extensions
summary: Do not add feature-specific logic to generic utility extensions.
body:
**Do not add feature-specific logic to generic utility extensions.** Create
feature-specific helpers instead.

title: Register Prefs in `browser_prefs.mm` on iOS
summary: iOS preference registration goes in `browser_prefs.mm`, not in arbitrary init methods.
body:
**iOS preference registration goes in `browser_prefs.mm`, not in arbitrary init
methods.**

summary: `Preferences.DAU.installationDate` resets after 14 days. Use `Preferences.P3A.installationDate` for persistent installation dates.
body:
**`Preferences.DAU.installationDate` resets after 14 days. Use
`Preferences.P3A.installationDate` for persistent installation dates.**

title: Wire Complete Observer/Bridge Chains
summary: When connecting C++ observers to Objective-C/Swift code, ensure the entire chain is wired: C++ observer → bridge object → Obj-C/Swift delegate.
body:
**When connecting C++ observers to Objective-C/Swift code, ensure the entire
chain is wired: C++ observer → bridge object → Obj-C/Swift delegate.** Missing
links in the chain are a common source of silent failures.

title: Use `raw_ptr<T>` for Stored Pointers in C++ Classes
summary: When a C++ class stores a pointer to another object, use `raw_ptr<T>` instead of raw `T*`.
body:
**When a C++ class stores a pointer to another object, use `raw_ptr<T>` instead
of raw `T*`.** This enables Chromium's pointer safety checks.

title: Use `NOTIMPLEMENTED()` for Potentially Reachable Code
summary: `NOTREACHED()` crashes in release builds. Use `NOTIMPLEMENTED()` for code paths that may be reached but are not yet implemented.
body:
**`NOTREACHED()` crashes in release builds. Use `NOTIMPLEMENTED()` for code
paths that may be reached but are not yet implemented.** Only use `NOTREACHED()`
when the code path should truly never execute.

title: Use Mojo `::Name_` Constants for Interface Registration
summary: When registering Mojo interfaces, use the `::Name_` constant from the generated interface, not hard-coded strings.
body:
**When registering Mojo interfaces, use the `::Name_` constant from the
generated interface, not hard-coded strings.**

title: Do Not Rely on iOS Caches Directory for Persistent State
summary: The iOS caches directory can be cleared by the system at any time.
body:
**The iOS caches directory can be cleared by the system at any time.** Do not
store state that must survive app restarts in the caches directory.

title: New Strings Go in `BraveStrings`, Not `SharedStrings.swift`
summary: Add new user-facing strings to `BraveStrings`, not `SharedStrings.swift`.
body:
**Add new user-facing strings to `BraveStrings`, not `SharedStrings.swift`.**
SharedStrings is for legacy/shared strings only.

title: Do Not Add New Functionality to the Legacy `Shared` Module
summary: The `Shared` module is legacy — do not add new functionality to it.
body:
**The `Shared` module is legacy — do not add new functionality to it.** If you
need a shared module for new code, create a new module instead. Existing
`Shared` code can still be used but should not be extended.

title: Tests Mirror Source Modules
summary: Test files should be organized to mirror the source module structure.
body:
**Test files should be organized to mirror the source module structure.** A
class in `BraveCore/Wallet/` should have tests in `BraveCoreTests/Wallet/`.

title: Export Pref Constants in Feature-Specific Headers
summary: iOS pref constants should be exported in feature-specific headers, not in a shared `pref_names_bridge.h`.
body:
**iOS pref constants should be exported in feature-specific headers, not in a
shared `pref_names_bridge.h`.** This reduces coupling and makes dependencies
explicit.

title: Mojom Wrappers Go in `ios/common`, Not `ios/browser`
summary: Mojom wrapper types belong in `ios/common/` because they are shared between browser and renderer processes.
body:
**Mojom wrapper types belong in `ios/common/` because they are shared between
browser and renderer processes.** Placing them in `ios/browser/` creates
unnecessary layering constraints.

title: Use `_bridge.h` for ObjC Wrappers, `_ios.h` for iOS Implementations
summary: Use the `_bridge.h` suffix for plain Objective-C wrapper headers that expose C++ types to Swift.
body:
**Use the `_bridge.h` suffix for plain Objective-C wrapper headers that expose
C++ types to Swift.** Use `_ios.h` for iOS-specific implementations of
cross-platform interfaces.

title: Use `Impl` Suffix for Concrete Implementations
summary: Name concrete implementations with the `Impl` suffix, not a platform suffix like `_ios`.
body:
**Name concrete implementations with the `Impl` suffix, not a platform suffix
like `_ios`.** For example: `BraveWalletServiceImpl`, not
`BraveWalletServiceIOS`.

title: Remove Dead Code and Debug Statements
summary: Remove all debug `print` statements and dead code before submitting.
body:
**Remove all debug `print` statements and dead code before submitting.** Use
`Logger` instead of `print` for any logging that should remain.

title: Preserve Accessibility Labels
summary: Always set accessibility labels on interactive elements.
body:
**Always set accessibility labels on interactive elements.** VoiceOver users
depend on these. When refactoring UI, verify that accessibility labels are
preserved.

title: Use `UIImage.prepareThumbnail(of:)` for Thumbnailing
summary: Use `UIImage.prepareThumbnail(of:)` for generating thumbnails instead of manual `UIGraphicsImageRenderer` resizing.
body:
**Use `UIImage.prepareThumbnail(of:)` for generating thumbnails instead of
manual `UIGraphicsImageRenderer` resizing.** The system method is optimized for
memory and performance.

title: Prefer CSS `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` Over JS Class Toggling
summary: For injected web content, use CSS `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` for dark mode support instead of toggling CSS classes via JavaScript.
body:
**For injected web content, use CSS `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` for
dark mode support instead of toggling CSS classes via JavaScript.**

title: Use `@_disfavoredOverload` + `@available(iOS, obsoleted:)` for Backporting
summary: When backporting newer APIs, use `@_disfavoredOverload` combined with `@available(iOS, obsoleted:)` to create transparent fallbacks that automatically disappear when the deployment target is raised.

title: Artificial Delays Require Comments
summary: Any use of `Task.sleep` or similar artificial delays must include a comment explaining why the delay is necessary.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - unexplained delay
try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 500_000_000)

title: Use `TimestampFormatStyle` for Duration Formatting
summary: Use `TimestampFormatStyle` or `Duration.formatted()` for displaying durations instead of manual string formatting.
body:
**Use `TimestampFormatStyle` or `Duration.formatted()` for displaying durations
instead of manual string formatting.**

title: Prefer Local Variables for Short-Lived Cancellables
summary: For Combine subscriptions that are only needed temporarily (e.g., waiting for a single value), use a local variable instead of storing the cancellable as a property.
body:
**For Combine subscriptions that are only needed temporarily (e.g., waiting for
a single value), use a local variable instead of storing the cancellable as a
property.** This prevents accumulation of dead subscriptions.

title: Check Delegate Before `withCheckedContinuation`
summary: When using `withCheckedContinuation` that depends on a delegate callback, verify the delegate is set before entering the continuation.
body:
**When using `withCheckedContinuation` that depends on a delegate callback,
verify the delegate is set before entering the continuation.** Otherwise the
continuation may never resume, hanging the task indefinitely.

title: Match Button Shapes to Nala Design System
summary: Buttons should use rounded rectangle shapes consistent with the Nala design system.
body:
**Buttons should use rounded rectangle shapes consistent with the Nala design
system.** Do not use fully rounded (capsule) or sharp-cornered buttons unless
the design specifically calls for it.

title: chromium_src iOS Overrides: Prefer Subclassing
summary: When overriding iOS Chromium classes via chromium_src, prefer subclassing over code duplication.
body:
**When overriding iOS Chromium classes via chromium_src, prefer subclassing over
code duplication.** Use the `#define`/`#include`/`#undef` pattern to substitute
Brave subclasses.

```cpp
// chromium_src/ios/chrome/browser/some_file.mm
#define ChromeViewController BraveViewController

#include <ios/chrome/browser/some_file.mm>

#undef ChromeViewController
```

**Always add blank lines around the `#define`/`#undef`-wrapped includes for
readability.**

title: Use GN Build Args for Platform-Specific Feature Defaults
summary: Use GN build arguments (not C++ source code) to set platform-specific feature defaults.
body:
**Use GN build arguments (not C++ source code) to set platform-specific feature
defaults.** This allows build-time configuration and reduces `#ifdef` clutter.

title: Include All iOS Test Targets in `brave_all_unit_tests`
summary: Every new iOS test target must be included in `brave_all_unit_tests`.
body:
**Every new iOS test target must be included in `brave_all_unit_tests`.** Tests
that are not included will never run on CI.

title: Feature Flag Names Must Match C++ Feature Names
summary: In iOS bridge headers, feature flag names must exactly match the C++ `base::Feature` names.
body:
**In iOS bridge headers, feature flag names must exactly match the C++
`base::Feature` names.** Mismatches cause silent failures where the flag appears
to work but doesn't actually control the feature.

title: Use `contentMode: .fill` or Size Constraints for Images
summary: Set explicit `contentMode` or size constraints on `UIImageView` and SwiftUI `Image` views.
body:
**Set explicit `contentMode` or size constraints on `UIImageView` and SwiftUI
`Image` views.** Without these, images may display at their natural size,
causing layout issues.

```swift
// SwiftUI
Image("icon")
  .resizable()
  .frame(maxWidth: 24, maxHeight: 24)

// UIKit
imageView.contentMode = .scaleAspectFill
```

title: Use `Label` for Icon-Only Buttons in SwiftUI
summary: Always use `Label` with `.labelStyle(.iconOnly)` for icon-only buttons.

title: Use Nala Design System Icons Over Apple's System Icons
summary: Use `Image(braveSystemName:)` with Nala (Leo) icons instead of Apple's `Image(systemName:)`.
body:
**Use `Image(braveSystemName:)` with Nala (Leo) icons instead of Apple's
`Image(systemName:)`.** Nala icons ensure visual consistency with the Brave
design system.

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - Apple system icon
Image(systemName: "trash")

// ✅ CORRECT - Nala design system icon
Image(braveSystemName: "leo.trash")
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - Apple system icon
Image(systemName: "trash")
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - Nala design system icon
Image(braveSystemName: "leo.trash")

title: Size Nala Icons Using Fonts, Not Frame
summary: Nala icons are custom SF Symbols and should be treated like font glyphs, not images.
body:
**Nala icons are custom SF Symbols and should be treated like font glyphs, not
images.** Size them with `.font()`, not `.resizable().frame()`.

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - treating icon like an image
Image(braveSystemName: "leo.trash")
  .resizable()
  .frame(width: 24, height: 24)

// ✅ CORRECT - sizing with font
Image(braveSystemName: "leo.trash")
  .font(.title3)
```
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - treating icon like an image
Image(braveSystemName: "leo.trash")
  .resizable()
  .frame(width: 24, height: 24)

title: Do Not Use Explicit Font Sizes
summary: UI must adhere to the user's dynamic font sizing preferences.
body:
**UI must adhere to the user's dynamic font sizing preferences.** Use semantic
font styles (`.subheadline`, `.body`, etc.). If a custom value must be used, use
`@ScaledMetric` in SwiftUI or `UIFontMetrics` in UIKit.

```swift
// ❌ WRONG - fixed font size ignores user preferences
Text("Hello World")
  .font(.system(size: 15))

// ✅ CORRECT - semantic font style
Text("Hello World")
  .font(.subheadline)

// ✅ CORRECT - scaled custom value
@ScaledMetric private var customSize = 15
Text("Hello World")
  .font(.system(size: customSize))
```

title: Do Not Initialize SwiftUI `@State` on `init`
summary: Do not assign `@State` properties in `init` using `State(wrappedValue:)`.

title: Avoid manual/computed SwiftUI Bindings
summary: Avoid using the `Binding(get:set:)` closure-based initializer to perform side-effects or transform state.

title: Don't Add `translateable="true"` on GRD Strings
summary: In `.grdp` string resource files, `translateable="true"` is the default.
body: **In `.grdp` string resource files, `translateable="true"` is the default.** Never add it explicitly. The tooling only looks for `translateable="false"` when excluding strings from translation. ---

title: Use Proper Ellipsis Characters in UI Strings
summary: In user-facing strings, use the proper Unicode ellipsis character (`…`) instead of three periods (`...`).
body: **In user-facing strings, use the proper Unicode ellipsis character (`…`) instead of three periods (`...`).** This is a standard typographic convention for UI text. ---

title: Provide Sufficient Context in Localization String Descriptions
summary: Localization string descriptions should contain enough context for translators who only see the description.
body: **Localization string descriptions should contain enough context for translators who only see the description.** For example, "History" alone might be ambiguous across languages (browser history vs. event history). Add specifics like "Title for the browser visits history section of a URL picker". For simple, self-evident strings where the meaning is unambiguous in any language (e.g., "Summary", "Settings", "Cancel"), a brief description is fine. **NEVER insist on verbose descriptions when the string speaks for itself.** Additional requirements for `desc` attributes: - **Never leave `desc` empty** — every `` element must have a non-empty description. - **Specify the UI element type** — include whether the string is a title, button label, description, tooltip, placeholder, menu item, etc. (e.g., `desc="Title for the about section"` not `desc="About section text"`). - **Disambiguate terms with multiple meanings** — words like "History" (browser vs. conversation), "Wallet" (crypto vs. payment), "Send" (where?) need qualification. - **Each description must be unique** — do not copy-paste the same `desc` across different strings that serve different purposes. - **Proofread descriptions** — typos in `desc` confuse translators and affect translation quality. ---

title: Use `I18nMixinLit` for Localization in Lit Components
summary: In Lit-based WebUI components, use `I18nMixinLit` instead of calling `loadTimeData.getString()` directly.
body: **In Lit-based WebUI components, use `I18nMixinLit` instead of calling `loadTimeData.getString()` directly.** The mixin provides consistent i18n patterns and is the standard approach. ---

title: Never Modify Upstream GRD/GRDP Files Directly
summary: Never add or modify strings in upstream Chromium GRD/GRDP files
body: **Never add or modify strings in upstream Chromium GRD/GRDP files** (e.g., `app/generated_resources.grd`, `app/settings_strings.grdp`, `components/browser_ui/strings/android/browser_ui_strings.grd`). These files are auto-replaced during every Chromium version bump, so any changes will be lost on the next rebase. To customize an upstream string: 1. Add a new string in the corresponding Brave GRD/GRDP file (e.g., `app/brave_generated_resources.grd`, `app/brave_settings_strings.grdp`, `browser/ui/android/strings/android_brave_strings.grd`). 2. Create a `chromium_src` override that `#undef`s the upstream `IDS_` constant and `#define`s it to your Brave-specific `IDS_` constant. ```cpp // chromium_src/chrome/browser/ui/webui/password_manager/password_manager_ui.cc #undef IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS #define IDS_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SYNCING_USERS \ IDS_BRAVE_PASSWORD_MANAGER_UI_EMPTY_STATE_SIGNEDOUT_USERS ``` ---

title: Use `grd_string_replacements.py` for Simple Upstream Text Substitutions
summary: For simple word/phrase substitutions across upstream strings in all locales, use `brave/script/lib/l10n/grd_string_replacements.py`
body: **For simple word/phrase substitutions across upstream strings in all locales, use `brave/script/lib/l10n/grd_string_replacements.py`** with `default_replacements` and run `pnpm run chromium_rebase_l10n`. This applies the replacement consistently across all localized versions without needing to manually edit GRD files or create chromium_src overrides. ---

title: Include `formatter_data="webui=X"` Matching the WebUI Component
summary: When adding strings to a WebUI GRDP file, include the `formatter_data="webui=ComponentName"` attribute.
body: **When adding strings to a WebUI GRDP file, include the `formatter_data="webui=ComponentName"` attribute.** The value must exactly match the WebUI component identifier so the build system generates the correct string constants for the right bundle. ```xml Welcome to Brave AI ``` ---
wrong:
<!-- ❌ WRONG - typo or mismatch means string won't be available in the component -->
<message name="IDS_CHAT_UI_WELCOME" desc="Welcome message" formatter_data="webui=AIChat">
right:
<!-- ✅ CORRECT - matches the AI Chat WebUI component -->
<message name="IDS_CHAT_UI_WELCOME" desc="Welcome message" formatter_data="webui=AiChat">
  Welcome to Brave AI
</message>

title: Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE Placeholder Names with Example Tags
summary: Placeholders in GRD/GRDP strings must have descriptive `name` attributes in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and include `<ex>` example tags
body: **Placeholders in GRD/GRDP strings must have descriptive `name` attributes in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and include `` example tags** showing translators what value will appear at runtime. ```xml Shredding will delete site data and close all $1example.com tabs. $1Learn more$2 Shredding will delete site data for $1. ``` ---
wrong:
<!-- ❌ WRONG - no descriptive name, no example -->
<message name="IDS_SHRED_CONFIRMATION" desc="Confirmation">
  Shredding will delete site data for <ph name="PH_1">$1</ph>.
</message>
right:
<!-- ✅ CORRECT - descriptive name and example -->
<message name="IDS_SHRED_CONFIRMATION" desc="Confirmation dialog for shredding site data">
  Shredding will delete site data and close all
  <ph name="SITE_NAME">$1<ex>example.com</ex></ph> tabs.
</message>

<!-- For link placeholders, use LINK_BEGIN/LINK_END pattern -->
<message name="IDS_LEARN_MORE" desc="Text with learn more link">
  <ph name="LINK_BEGIN">$1</ph>Learn more<ph name="LINK_END">$2</ph>
</message>

title: Capitalization Consistency Across Feature Strings
summary: All strings within a single feature or UI surface must use a consistent capitalization style.
body: **All strings within a single feature or UI surface must use a consistent capitalization style.** Do not mix title case ("Background Image") and sentence case ("Brave backgrounds") within the same group of UI controls at the same hierarchy level. - **Title case** for: page titles, section headers, button labels, menu items - **Sentence case** for: descriptions, body text, tooltips, helper text ---

title: UI Text Voice and Style Conventions
summary: Follow these conventions for user-facing string text:
body: **Follow these conventions for user-facing string text:** - **Use "Brave's" instead of "our"** — e.g., "access Brave's premium products" not "access our premium products" - **Use "and more" instead of "etc."** — e.g., "bookmarks, passwords, and more" not "bookmarks, passwords, etc." - **Match established feature terminology** — e.g., Shields uses "up/down" not "on/off" (`"with Shields up"` not `"with Shields on"`). Check existing strings for a feature's vocabulary before adding new ones. - **Use natural word order around placeholders** — test by substituting an example value and reading the sentence aloud - **Avoid possessive constructions** — prefer "the content of this page" over "this page's contents" for better translatability - **Be explicit about data-sharing actions** — "send your tabs to Brave AI" not just "send your tabs" (where?) ---

title: Never Add Unused Strings to GRD/GRDP Files
summary: Only add strings to GRD/GRDP files when they are actively referenced in the codebase.
body: **Only add strings to GRD/GRDP files when they are actively referenced in the codebase.** Every string in a GRD/GRDP file gets sent to translators and translated into all supported languages, which costs time and money. If a string is no longer used after a refactor, remove it. When reviewing string additions, verify the `IDS_` constant is actually used in the code. ---

title: Replace Upstream Product Names with Brave Equivalents During Rebases
summary: During Chromium rebases, review all new strings in upstream GRD/GRDP files for Google product references
body: **During Chromium rebases, review all new strings in upstream GRD/GRDP files for Google product references** (Gemini, Google Pay, Chrome, etc.) that need to be replaced with Brave equivalents. New user-facing strings introduced by rebases should be reviewed to ensure they show correct Brave branding. Also verify correct product name usage: "Brave Wallet" refers specifically to the cryptocurrency wallet, not general autofill/payment card features. ---

title: Avoid Dynamic String Key Construction in `getLocale()`
summary: Never dynamically construct string keys for `getLocale()` calls.
body: **Never dynamically construct string keys for `getLocale()` calls.** This makes static analysis impossible, prevents dead string detection, and breaks if key formats change. ```tsx // ❌ WRONG - dynamic key construction getLocale(`CHAT_UI_${model.key.toUpperCase().replaceAll('-', '_')}_SUBTITLE`) // ✅ CORRECT - explicit string reference getLocale(S.CHAT_UI_CLAUDE_SUBTITLE) // ✅ ALSO CORRECT - data source provides the string or key model.description // provided by server API / mojom struct ``` ---
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - dynamic key construction
getLocale(`CHAT_UI_${model.key.toUpperCase().replaceAll('-', '_')}_SUBTITLE`)
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - explicit string reference
getLocale(S.CHAT_UI_CLAUDE_SUBTITLE)

// ✅ ALSO CORRECT - data source provides the string or key
model.description // provided by server API / mojom struct

title: Build Links in UI, Not in Localized Strings
summary: When a localized string needs a clickable link, build the link element in the UI (TypeScript/HTML) and pass the URL separately

title: Punctuation Rules for Settings Toggle Descriptions
summary: Settings toggle descriptions follow specific punctuation rules:
body: **Settings toggle descriptions follow specific punctuation rules:** - **Single-sentence descriptions** should NOT end with a period. - **Multi-sentence descriptions** SHOULD end with a period on the last sentence. ---

title: String Text Must Be Complete and Grammatically Correct
summary: User-facing strings must be complete sentences (not truncated), grammatically correct, and use proper punctuation.
body: **User-facing strings must be complete sentences (not truncated), grammatically correct, and use proper punctuation.** String reviewers verify: - Sentences are not cut off mid-thought - Compound adjectives are hyphenated (e.g., "non-compatible" not "non compatible") - Prepositions are appropriate for context (e.g., "in" vs. "on" for UI locations) This matters because translators use the English source as a reference, and errors propagate to translations. ---

title: Include UI Screenshots When Adding or Modifying Strings
summary: When a PR adds or modifies user-facing strings, the developer must include a screenshot of the affected UI in the PR description.
body:
**When a PR adds or modifies user-facing strings, the developer must include a
screenshot of the affected UI in the PR description.** This allows string
reviewers to verify the string in context — checking for truncation,
capitalization consistency, layout issues, and correct terminology. Screenshots
should show the actual rendered UI, not just the GRD/GRDP diff.

Do not add screenshots as inline code comments. Add them to the PR description
body.

See also: [Brave Style Guide](./style-guide.md) for voice, capitalization,
punctuation, and product naming rules that apply to all user-facing strings.

summary: Before creating a custom React component, check whether Leo already provides it. Custom re-implementations add maintenance burden and are often less accessible than the Leo originals.
right:
// ✅ CORRECT - Leo Tooltip
import Tooltip from '@brave/leo/react/tooltip'
;<Tooltip text='Helpful hint'>
  <Button>Hover me</Button>
</Tooltip>

docTitle: Nala / Leo Design System Best Practices
title: Don't Create Intermediate Color Tokens — Use Nala Tokens Directly
summary: When referencing Nala/Leo color tokens in C++ color mixers, use the Nala token directly at the call site instead of creating an intermediate `kColor*` token that just maps to it.

title: Patches Must Contain Only Functional Changes
summary: Patches should contain only the minimal functional changes needed.
body:
**Patches should contain only the minimal functional changes needed.** Never add
comments, empty lines, whitespace changes, or any other non-functional
modifications. Leave whitespace intact to minimize diff size. Unnecessary
changes make patches harder to review and more likely to conflict during
Chromium upgrades.

title: No Multiline Patches - Use Defines
summary: Never create multiline patches. Use `#define` macros or chromium_src overrides instead.
body:
**Never create multiline patches. Use `#define` macros or chromium_src overrides
instead.**

**NEVER apply this restriction to plaster-generated patches:** they are
multiline by design. **NEVER introduce new macros that edit upstream code**
([PLSTR-003](./plaster.md#PLSTR-003)).

title: Use `include` for Extensible Patches
summary: When a patch adds to a list or block, use an `include` directive to make the patch extensible.
body:
**When a patch adds to a list or block, use an `include` directive to make the
patch extensible.** This way additional items can be added in brave-core without
modifying the patch.

title: Patches Should Use `define` for Extensibility
summary: Patches should use `#define` macros to be extensible.
wrong:
// ❌ WRONG - patching inline code directly
+  if (permission == AUTOPLAY) return true;

title: Patch Style Guidelines
summary: - **Keep patches to one line** even if it violates lint character line limits (lint doesn't run on patched files) - **In XML patches, use HTML comments** (`<!-- -->`) instead of deleting lines to reduce the diff - **Minimize line modifications** - put additions on separate lines to avoid modifying existing lines - **Match existing code exactly** when possible so patches auto-resolve during updates
body:
- **Keep patches to one line** even if it violates lint character line limits
  (lint doesn't run on patched files)
- **In XML patches, use HTML comments** (`<!-- -->`) instead of deleting lines
  to reduce the diff
- **Minimize line modifications** - put additions on separate lines to avoid
  modifying existing lines
- **Match existing code exactly** when possible so patches auto-resolve during

```xml
<!-- ❌ WRONG - deleting XML elements -->
-<LinearLayout ...>
-  ...
-</LinearLayout>

<!-- ✅ CORRECT - commenting out -->

+-->
```
